```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Decode base64-encoded TFLite model from Colab training."""
import base64
from pathlib import Path

SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).parent
INPUT_FILE = SCRIPT_DIR / "hey_daisy_base64.txt"
OUTPUT_FILE = SCRIPT_DIR / "hey_daisy.tflite"

def main():
    with open(INPUT_FILE, "r") as f:
        b64_string = f.read().strip()

    model_bytes = base64.b64decode(b64_string)

    with open(OUTPUT_FILE, "wb") as f:
        f.write(model_bytes)

    print(f"Decoded {len(b64_string)} base64 chars -> {len(model_bytes)} bytes")
    print(f"Saved: {OUTPUT_FILE}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

   265→bool initInterpreter() {
   266→  // Get model
   267→  const tflite::Model* model = tflite::GetModel(model_data);
   268→  if (model->version() != TFLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION) {
   269→    Serial.printf("Model version mismatch: %d vs %d\n",
   270→                  model->version(), TFLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION);
   271→    return false;
   272→  }
   273→
   274→  // Create allocator for resource variables (streaming model state)
   275→  var_allocator = tflite::MicroAllocator::Create(var_arena, VAR_ARENA_SIZE);
   276→  if (!var_allocator) {
   277→    Serial.println("Failed to create var allocator");
   278→    return false;
   279→  }
   280→
   281→  // Create resource variables container
   282→  resource_vars = tflite::MicroResourceVariables::Create(var_allocator, MAX_RESOURCE_VARS);
   283→  if (!resource_vars) {
   284→    Serial.println("Failed to create resource variables");
   285→    return false;
   286→  }
   287→
   288→  // Create interpreter WITH resource variables support
   289→  static tflite::MicroInterpreter static_interpreter(
   290→      model, resolver, tensor_arena, TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE, resource_vars);
   291→  interpreter = &static_interpreter;
   292→
   293→  // Allocate tensors
   294→  if (interpreter->AllocateTensors() != kTfLiteOk) {
   295→    Serial.println("AllocateTensors failed");
   296→    return false;
   297→  }
   298→
   299→  // Get input/output tensors
   300→  input_tensor = interpreter->input(0);
   301→  output_tensor = interpreter->output(0);
   302→
   303→  if (!input_tensor || !output_tensor) {
   304→    Serial.println("Failed to get tensors");
   305→    return false;
   306→  }
   307→
   308→  return true;
   309→}

   381→bool captureAudio() {
   382→  // Only read if we have space in buffer
   383→  int space_available = AUDIO_BUFFER_SIZE - audio_buffer_pos;
   384→  if (space_available < 256) {
   385→    return true;  // Buffer has data, let it be processed first
   386→  }
   387→
   388→  // Read smaller chunks more frequently for smoother audio
   389→  int samples_to_read = min(256, space_available);
   390→  size_t bytes_read;
   391→  if (i2s_read(I2S_NUM_0, i2s_buffer, samples_to_read * 4, &bytes_read, 10) != ESP_OK) {
   392→    return false;
   393→  }
   394→
   395→  int samples = bytes_read / 4;
   396→
   397→  // Track audio levels for debug
   398→  static int audio_debug = 0;
   399→  int32_t max_sample = 0;
   400→
   401→  for (int i = 0; i < samples; i++) {
   402→    // Convert 32-bit I2S to 16-bit
   403→    // INMP441 outputs 24-bit in MSB of 32-bit word, shift right to get 16-bit
   404→    int32_t sample = i2s_buffer[i] >> 14;  // >>14 for moderate gain
   405→    audio_buffer[audio_buffer_pos++] = constrain(sample, -32768, 32767);
   406→
   407→    if (abs(sample) > max_sample) max_sample = abs(sample);
   408→  }
   409→
   410→#if DEBUG_FEATURES
   411→  if (++audio_debug >= 300) {
   412→    audio_debug = 0;
   413→    Serial.printf("Audio: amp=%ld, buf=%d\n", max_sample, audio_buffer_pos);
   414→  }
   415→#endif
   416→
   417→  return true;
   418→}

   420→float runInference() {
   421→  // Copy 3 frames of features to input tensor
   422→  int total_features = FEATURE_FRAMES * FEATURE_BINS;  // 3 * 40 = 120
   423→
   424→  // Debug: print quant params once
   425→  static bool printed_params = false;
   426→  if (!printed_params) {
   427→    printed_params = true;
   428→    Serial.printf("\n=== INFERENCE DEBUG ===\n");
   429→    Serial.printf("Input type=%d, scale=%.6f, zp=%d\n",
   430→      input_tensor->type, input_tensor->params.scale, input_tensor->params.zero_point);
   431→    Serial.printf("Output type=%d, scale=%.6f, zp=%d\n",
   432→      output_tensor->type, output_tensor->params.scale, output_tensor->params.zero_point);
   433→    Serial.printf("Input bytes=%d, Output bytes=%d\n",
   434→      input_tensor->bytes, output_tensor->bytes);
   435→  }
   436→
   437→  if (input_tensor->type == kTfLiteInt8) {
   438→    int8_t* input_data = input_tensor->data.int8;
   439→
   440→    // Use ESPHome's proven formula directly
   441→    for (int i = 0; i < total_features; i++) {
   442→      int32_t scaled = ((int32_t)feature_buffer[i] * 256 + 333) / 666 - 128;
   443→      input_data[i] = constrain(scaled, -128, 127);
   444→    }
   445→
   446→    // Debug: show first few input values once
   447→    static int input_debug = 0;
   448→    if (++input_debug == 50) {
   449→      Serial.printf("Input[0-5]: %d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d\n",
   450→        input_data[0], input_data[1], input_data[2],
   451→        input_data[3], input_data[4], input_data[5]);
   452→    }
   453→  } else {
   454→    // Float model
   455→    float* input_data = input_tensor->data.f;
   456→    for (int i = 0; i < total_features; i++) {
   457→      input_data[i] = feature_buffer[i] / 25.6f;
   458→    }
   459→  }
   460→
   461→  // Run inference
   462→  if (interpreter->Invoke() != kTfLiteOk) {
   463→    Serial.println("Invoke failed");
   464→    return 0.0f;
   465→  }
   466→
   467→  // Get output probability
   468→  float probability;
   469→
   470→  // Debug: show raw output once
   471→  static int out_debug = 0;
   472→
   473→  if (output_tensor->type == kTfLiteUInt8) {
   474→    uint8_t output_value = output_tensor->data.uint8[0];
   475→    probability = (output_value - output_tensor->params.zero_point) *
   476→                  output_tensor->params.scale;
   477→    if (++out_debug == 50) {
   478→      Serial.printf("Raw output uint8=%u, prob=%.4f\n", output_value, probability);
   479→    }
   480→  } else if (output_tensor->type == kTfLiteInt8) {
   481→    int8_t output_value = output_tensor->data.int8[0];
   482→    probability = (output_value - output_tensor->params.zero_point) *
   483→                  output_tensor->params.scale;
   484→    if (++out_debug == 50) {
   485→      Serial.printf("Raw output int8=%d, prob=%.4f\n", output_value, probability);
   486→    }
   487→  } else {
   488→    probability = output_tensor->data.f[0];
   489→    if (++out_debug == 50) {
   490→      Serial.printf("Raw output float=%.4f\n", probability);
   491→    }
   492→  }
   493→
   494→  return probability;
   495→}
   496→
   497→bool detectWakeword(float probability) {
   498→  // Add to sliding window
   499→  probability_window[window_pos] = probability;
   500→  window_pos = (window_pos + 1) % SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;
   501→
   502→  if (window_pos == 0) {
   503→    window_filled = true;
   504→  }
   505→
   506→  // Don't trigger until window is filled
   507→  if (!window_filled) {
   508→    return false;
   509→  }
   510→
   511→  // Calculate average probability
   512→  float avg = 0.0f;
   513→  for (int i = 0; i < SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
   514→    avg += probability_window[i];
   515→  }
   516→  avg /= SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;
   517→
   518→  // Log probability (always show for debugging)
   519→  static int log_count = 0;
   520→  if (probability > 0.01f || ++log_count >= 100) {
   521→    Serial.printf("prob: %.4f, avg: %.4f\n", probability, avg);
   522→    log_count = 0;
   523→  }
   524→
   525→  return avg >= PROBABILITY_CUTOFF;
   526→}

<cell id="cell-2"># Cell 2: Initialize model
from continue_tts import Continue1Model
import torch

print(f"CUDA available: {torch.cuda.is_available()}")
print("Loading Continue-TTS model (~7GB GPU RAM)...")

model = Continue1Model(
    model_name="SVECTOR-CORPORATION/Continue-TTS",
    max_model_len=2048
)

print("Model loaded!")</cell id="cell-2">

Outputs are too large to include. Use Bash with: cat <notebook_path> | jq '.cells[2].outputs'
<cell id="cell-3"># Cell 3: Available voices
VOICES = {
    'nova': 'Female - Conversational and natural',
    'aurora': 'Female - Warm and friendly',
    'stellar': 'Female - Energetic and bright',
    'luna': 'Female - Soft and gentle',
    'ember': 'Female - Warm and engaging',
    'atlas': 'Male - Deep and authoritative',
    'orion': 'Male - Friendly and casual',
    'phoenix': 'Male - Dynamic and expressive',
}

print("Available voices:")
for voice, desc in VOICES.items():
    print(f"  {voice:10} - {desc}")</cell id="cell-3">
<cell id="cell-4"># Cell 4: Generate "Hey Daisy" samples with different voices
import wave
import os
from pathlib import Path

OUTPUT_DIR = Path('generated_audio')
OUTPUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Text variations to generate
TEXTS = [
    "Hey Daisy",
    "Hey Daisy!",
    "Hey Daisy?",
]

# Voices to test (subset for speed)
TEST_VOICES = ['nova', 'aurora', 'atlas', 'orion']

generated_files = []

print(f"Generating {len(TEXTS)} texts x {len(TEST_VOICES)} voices = {len(TEXTS) * len(TEST_VOICES)} samples\n")

for voice in TEST_VOICES:
    for i, text in enumerate(TEXTS):
        filename = OUTPUT_DIR / f"hey_daisy_{voice}_{i}.wav"
        print(f"  Generating: {voice} - '{text}'")
        
        try:
            audio_chunks = model.generate_speech(
                prompt=text,
                voice=voice,
                temperature=0.6,
                top_p=0.8,
                repetition_penalty=1.3
            )
            
            with wave.open(str(filename), "wb") as wf:
                wf.setnchannels(1)
                wf.setsampwidth(2)
                wf.setframerate(24000)
                for chunk in audio_chunks:
                    wf.writeframes(chunk)
            
            generated_files.append((str(filename), voice, text))
            print(f"    Saved: {filename}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"    Error: {e}")

print(f"\nGenerated {len(generated_files)} audio files")</cell id="cell-4">
<cell id="cell-5"># Cell 5: Audio playback widgets
from IPython.display import Audio, display, HTML

print("Generated samples - click to play:\n")

for filepath, voice, text in generated_files:
    display(HTML(f"<b>{voice}</b>: '{text}'"))
    display(Audio(filepath))
    print()</cell id="cell-5">

print("Generating 'Hey Daisy' with ALL 8 voices for comparison...\n")

all_voices_files = []
text = "Hey Daisy"

for voice in VOICES.keys():
    filename = OUTPUT_DIR / f"hey_daisy_ALL_{voice}.wav"
    print(f"  {voice}...")
    
    try:
        audio_chunks = model.generate_speech(
            prompt=text,
            voice=voice,
            temperature=0.6,
            top_p=0.8
        )
        
        with wave.open(str(filename), "wb") as wf:
            wf.setnchannels(1)
            wf.setsampwidth(2)
            wf.setframerate(24000)
            for chunk in audio_chunks:
                wf.writeframes(chunk)
        
        all_voices_files.append((str(filename), voice))
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"    Error: {e}")

print("\n" + "="*50)
print("ALL VOICES - 'Hey Daisy'")
print("="*50 + "\n")

for filepath, voice in all_voices_files:
    desc = VOICES[voice]
    display(HTML(f"<b>{voice}</b> ({desc})"))
    display(Audio(filepath))
    print()</cell id="cell-6">
<cell id="cell-7"># Cell 7: Test with emotion tags
print("Testing emotion tags...\n")

emotion_texts = [
    ("Hey Daisy! <laugh>", "With laugh"),
    ("<sigh> Hey Daisy", "With sigh"),
    ("Hey Daisy? <gasp>", "With gasp"),
]

voice = "nova"
emotion_files = []

for text, label in emotion_texts:
    filename = OUTPUT_DIR / f"hey_daisy_emotion_{label.replace(' ', '_')}.wav"
    print(f"  Generating: '{text}'")
    
    try:
        audio_chunks = model.generate_speech(
            prompt=text,
            voice=voice,
            temperature=0.7
        )
        
        with wave.open(str(filename), "wb") as wf:
            wf.setnchannels(1)
            wf.setsampwidth(2)
            wf.setframerate(24000)
            for chunk in audio_chunks:
                wf.writeframes(chunk)
        
        emotion_files.append((str(filename), label, text))
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"    Error: {e}")

print("\nEmotion samples:")
for filepath, label, text in emotion_files:
    display(HTML(f"<b>{label}</b>: '{text}'"))
    display(Audio(filepath))
    print()</cell id="cell-7">
<cell id="cell-8"># Cell 8: Custom text generation
from IPython.display import clear_output
import ipywidgets as widgets

# Text input
text_input = widgets.Text(
    value='Hey Daisy, what time is it?',
    placeholder='Enter text to speak',
    description='Text:',
    layout=widgets.Layout(width='80%')
)

# Voice selector
voice_dropdown = widgets.Dropdown(
    options=list(VOICES.keys()),
    value='nova',
    description='Voice:',
)

# Generate button
generate_btn = widgets.Button(
    description='Generate Speech',
    button_style='primary'
)

# Output area
output = widgets.Output()

def on_generate(btn):
    with output:
        clear_output()
        text = text_input.value
        voice = voice_dropdown.value
        
        print(f"Generating: '{text}' with voice '{voice}'...")
        
        try:
            filename = OUTPUT_DIR / "custom_output.wav"
            audio_chunks = model.generate_speech(
                prompt=text,
                voice=voice,
                temperature=0.6,
                top_p=0.8
            )
            
            with wave.open(str(filename), "wb") as wf:
                wf.setnchannels(1)
                wf.setsampwidth(2)
                wf.setframerate(24000)
                for chunk in audio_chunks:
                    wf.writeframes(chunk)
            
            print("Done! Play below:")
            display(Audio(str(filename)))
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error: {e}")

generate_btn.on_click(on_generate)

print("Custom TTS Generator")
print("="*40)
display(text_input)
display(voice_dropdown)
display(generate_btn)
display(output)</cell id="cell-8">
<cell id="cell-9"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Summary

**Continue-TTS Features:**
- 8 diverse voices (5 female, 3 male)
- Emotion tags: `<laugh>`, `<sigh>`, `<gasp>`, etc.
- 24kHz high-quality audio
- ~200ms latency on GPU

**For wake word training:**
- Could replace/supplement XTTS for more voice variety
- Built-in voices = no speaker reference needed
- Apache 2.0 license</cell id="cell-9">

Updated cell cell-3 with # Cell 3: Load SNAC decoder and define generation function
from snac import SNAC
import numpy as np

# Load SNAC audio decoder
snac = SNAC.from_pretrained("hubertsiuzdak/snac_24khz").to(model.device)

# Available voices
VOICES = {
    'nova': 'Female - Conversational and natural',
    'aurora': 'Female - Warm and friendly', 
    'stellar': 'Female - Energetic and bright',
    'luna': 'Female - Soft and gentle',
    'ember': 'Female - Warm and engaging',
    'atlas': 'Male - Deep and authoritative',
    'orion': 'Male - Friendly and casual',
    'phoenix': 'Male - Dynamic and expressive',
}

# Special tokens for TTS
START_TOKEN = torch.tensor([[128259]], dtype=torch.int64)
END_TOKENS = torch.tensor([[128009, 128260, 128261, 128257]], dtype=torch.int64)
TTS_STOP_TOKEN = 49158

def generate_speech(text, voice='nova', temperature=0.6, top_p=0.8, max_tokens=1200):
    """Generate speech from text using Continue-TTS"""
    # Format prompt
    adapted_prompt = f"{voice}: {text}"
    prompt_tokens = tokenizer(adapted_prompt, return_tensors="pt")
    
    # Build input with special tokens
    input_ids = torch.cat([
        START_TOKEN,
        prompt_tokens.input_ids,
        END_TOKENS
    ], dim=1).to(model.device)
    
    # Generate audio tokens
    with torch.no_grad():
        outputs = model.generate(
            input_ids,
            max_new_tokens=max_tokens,
            temperature=temperature,
            top_p=top_p,
            repetition_penalty=1.3,
            eos_token_id=TTS_STOP_TOKEN,
            do_sample=True
        )
    
    # Extract generated tokens (skip input)
    generated = outputs[0][input_ids.shape[1]:]
    
    # Parse SNAC codes from tokens
    # Continue-TTS uses token offsets: 128266 for layer 0, etc.
    code_offsets = [128266, 128266 + 4096, 128266 + 8192]
    
    codes = [[], [], []]
    for token in generated.tolist():
        for i, offset in enumerate(code_offsets):
            if offset <= token < offset + 4096:
                codes[i].append(token - offset)
                break
    
    # Decode with SNAC
    if codes[0]:
        # Pad to match lengths (SNAC expects specific ratios)
        min_len = min(len(codes[0]), len(codes[1]) // 2, len(codes[2]) // 4)
        if min_len > 0:
            codes_tensor = [
                torch.tensor(codes[0][:min_len], device=model.device).unsqueeze(0),
                torch.tensor(codes[1][:min_len*2], device=model.device).unsqueeze(0),
                torch.tensor(codes[2][:min_len*4], device=model.device).unsqueeze(0),
            ]
            
            with torch.no_grad():
                audio = snac.decode(codes_tensor)
            
            return audio.squeeze().cpu().numpy()
    
    return None

print(f"SNAC decoder loaded")
print(f"\nAvailable voices:")
for voice, desc in VOICES.items():
    print(f"  {voice:10} - {desc}")
```

SAMPLE_RATE = 24000

        print(f"  Generating: {voice} - '{text}'")
        
        try:
            audio = generate_speech(text, voice=voice)
            
            if audio is not None:
                # Convert to int16 for WAV
                audio_int16 = (audio * 32767).astype(np.int16)
                
                with wave.open(str(filename), "wb") as wf:
                    wf.setnchannels(1)
                    wf.setsampwidth(2)
                    wf.setframerate(SAMPLE_RATE)
                    wf.writeframes(audio_int16.tobytes())
                
                generated_files.append((str(filename), voice, text))
                print(f"    Saved: {filename}")
            else:
                print(f"    Warning: No audio generated")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"    Error: {e}")

print(f"\nGenerated {len(generated_files)} audio files")

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">
<cell id="cell-1"># Cell 1: Install dependencies

# Install audio-metadata fork (required)
!pip install -q 'git+https://github.com/whatsnowplaying/audio-metadata@d4ebb238e6a401bb1a5aaaac60c9e2b3cb30929f'

# Install pymicro-features fork with correct API (ProcessSamples method)
!pip install -q 'git+https://github.com/puddly/pymicro-features@puddly/minimum-cpp-version'

# Clone and install microWakeWord
!git clone --quiet https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord
!pip install -q -e ./microWakeWord

print("microWakeWord installed!")</cell id="cell-1">

<cell id="cell-2"># Cell 2: Install TTS engines (Piper + XTTS-v2)
!git clone --quiet https://github.com/rhasspy/piper-sample-generator

# Download Piper TTS model
!mkdir -p piper-sample-generator/models
!wget -q -O piper-sample-generator/models/en_US-libritts_r-medium.pt \
    'https://github.com/rhasspy/piper-sample-generator/releases/download/v2.0.0/en_US-libritts_r-medium.pt'

!pip install -q piper-tts
!pip install torchcodec --index-url=https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126

# Install XTTS-v2 for human-like voice cloning
!pip uninstall --yes torch torchaudio torchvision torchtext torchdata
!pip install -q torch==2.8.0 torchdata torchvision==0.23.0 torchaudio==2.8.0 
!pip install -q coqui-tts

print("Piper TTS + XTTS-v2 installed!")</cell id="cell-2">

<cell id="cell-8"># Cell 6: Generate full training dataset (4X SCALED - Piper + XTTS with ALL TED samples)
import subprocess
import shutil
import torch
import librosa
import soundfile as sf
import urllib.request

training_dir = GENERATED_DIR / 'training'

# Clean up existing samples for fresh batch
if training_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(training_dir)
training_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

#=============================================================================
# PART 1: Download ALL TED speaker samples (8 speakers × 10 samples = 80 total)
#=============================================================================
speaker_voices_dir = WORK_DIR / 'speaker_voices'
speaker_voices_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# All 8 speakers, each with 10 samples
TED_SPEAKERS = ['BillGates', 'DaphneKoller', 'FeiFeiLi', 'GeorgeTakei', 
                'JaneGoodall', 'SalmanKhan', 'StephenHawking', 'StephenWolfram']
SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER = 10

speaker_files = []
print(f"Downloading ALL TED speaker samples ({len(TED_SPEAKERS)} speakers × {SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER} samples = {len(TED_SPEAKERS) * SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER} total)...")

for speaker in TED_SPEAKERS:
    for sample_idx in range(SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER):
        url = f'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/audio-samples/audio-samples.github.io/master/samples/mp3/ted_speakers/{speaker}/sample-{sample_idx}.mp3'
        mp3_path = speaker_voices_dir / f'ted_{speaker}_{sample_idx}.mp3'
        wav_path = speaker_voices_dir / f'ted_{speaker}_{sample_idx}.wav'
        
        if not wav_path.exists():
            try:
                urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, mp3_path)
                audio, sr = librosa.load(mp3_path, sr=16000, mono=True)
                if len(audio) > 6 * 16000:
                    audio = audio[:6 * 16000]  # 6 seconds for XTTS
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio, 16000)
                mp3_path.unlink()
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  ✗ {speaker}/sample-{sample_idx}: {e}")
                continue
        speaker_files.append(str(wav_path))
    print(f"  ✓ {speaker} ({SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER} samples)")

print(f"  Total: {len(speaker_files)} voice references\n")

#=============================================================================
# PART 2: Initialize XTTS-v2
#=============================================================================
print("Loading XTTS-v2 model...")
from TTS.api import TTS
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
xtts = TTS("tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2").to(device)
print(f"  XTTS-v2 loaded on {device}\n")

#=============================================================================
# PART 3: Generate samples with BOTH TTS engines
#=============================================================================
PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR = 100   # Piper: fast, diverse synthetic voices

# XTTS: Use subset of speakers per variation (randomly sample to avoid 1600 XTTS samples)
XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR = 20    # Use 20 random voice refs per variation

import random
random.seed(42)

total_piper = len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR
total_xtts = len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR
total_samples = total_piper + total_xtts

print(f"Generating {total_samples} samples:")
print(f"  Piper: {total_piper} samples ({PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR}/variation)")
print(f"  XTTS:  {total_xtts} samples ({XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR} voices/variation from {len(speaker_files)} available)")
print()

# --- PIPER GENERATION ---
print("PIPER TTS generation...")
for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}'")
    temp_dir = GENERATED_DIR / f'temp_piper_{i}'
    temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    subprocess.run([
        'python3', 'piper-sample-generator/generate_samples.py',
        variation,
        '--max-samples', str(PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR),
        '--batch-size', '10',
        '--output-dir', str(temp_dir),
        '--model', 'piper-sample-generator/models/en_US-libritts_r-medium.pt'
    ], capture_output=True)
    
    for wav in temp_dir.glob('*.wav'):
        new_name = f"piper_var{i}_{wav.name}"
        shutil.move(str(wav), str(training_dir / new_name))
    temp_dir.rmdir()

# --- XTTS GENERATION ---
print("\nXTTS-v2 generation (human-like voices from 80 TED samples)...")
for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    # Randomly sample voices for this variation
    selected_voices = random.sample(speaker_files, XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR)
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}' ({len(selected_voices)} voices)")
    
    for j, speaker_wav in enumerate(selected_voices):
        speaker_name = Path(speaker_wav).stem
        filename = training_dir / f"xtts_var{i}_{speaker_name}.wav"
        try:
            xtts.tts_to_file(
                text=variation,
                file_path=str(filename),
                speaker_wav=speaker_wav,
                language="en"
            )
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"    ✗ {speaker_name}: {e}")

sample_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))
print(f"\n✓ Generated {sample_count} total samples")
print(f"  Piper (synthetic): ~{total_piper}")
print(f"  XTTS (human-like): ~{total_xtts} (from {len(speaker_files)} voice references)")</cell id="cell-8">

# AudioSet was converted to parquet - use datasets library
!pip install -q datasets soundfile

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

AUDIOSET_DIR = AUGMENTATION_DIR / 'audioset'
AUDIOSET_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Check if we already have audio files
existing = list(AUDIOSET_DIR.glob('*.wav'))
if len(existing) >= 100:
    print(f"AudioSet already has {len(existing)} samples, skipping download")
else:
    try:
        from datasets import load_dataset
        import soundfile as sf
        print("Loading AudioSet subset via datasets library...")
        
        # Load balanced subset with streaming
        ds = load_dataset(
            "agkphysics/AudioSet", 
            split="train",
            streaming=True,
            trust_remote_code=True
        )
        
        # Save first 500 audio samples as wav files
        count = 0
        max_samples = 500
        
        for sample in ds:
            if count >= max_samples:
                break
            try:
                audio = sample['audio']
                wav_path = AUDIOSET_DIR / f"audioset_{count:04d}.wav"
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio['array'], audio['sampling_rate'])
                count += 1
                if count % 100 == 0:
                    print(f"  Saved {count}/{max_samples} samples")
            except Exception:
                continue  # Skip problematic samples
        
        print(f"Done! Saved {count} background audio samples")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"AudioSet loading failed: {e}")
        print("Background augmentation will use MIT impulse responses only.")</cell id="cell-12">

<cell id="cell-16"># Cell 11: Generate spectrogram features (with TESTING set)
from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips
from microwakeword.audio.spectrograms import SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja import RaggedMmap
import shutil
import os
import time

# Structure expected by microwakeword:
# features_dir/training/*_mmap/
# features_dir/validation/*_mmap/
# features_dir/testing/*_mmap/
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Create proper directory structure with _mmap suffix
train_base_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'training'
val_base_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'validation'
test_base_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'testing'
train_features_dir = train_base_dir / 'positive_mmap'
val_features_dir = val_base_dir / 'positive_mmap'
test_features_dir = test_base_dir / 'positive_mmap'

# Verify audio files exist
wav_files = list(training_dir.glob('*.wav'))
print(f"Found {len(wav_files)} wav files in {training_dir}")

# Clean up old features COMPLETELY
for d in [train_base_dir, val_base_dir, test_base_dir]:
    if d.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(d)
        print(f"  Deleted: {d}")
os.sync()
time.sleep(1)

# Create directories
for d in [train_features_dir, val_features_dir, test_features_dir]:
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

#=============================================================================
# Split: 80% train, 10% validation, 10% test
# We'll use two Clips objects with different seeds to create the splits
#=============================================================================

# Generate TRAINING features (with augmentation) - 80% of data
print("\nGenerating TRAINING features (80% of data, with augmentation)...")
train_clips = Clips(
    input_directory=str(training_dir),
    file_pattern='*.wav',
    max_clip_duration_s=None,
    remove_silence=False,
    random_split_seed=42,
    split_count=0.2  # 20% held out (will be split into val + test)
)
print(f"  Train split: {len(train_clips.split_clips['train'])} clips")

train_spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration(
    clips=train_clips,
    augmenter=augmentation,
    slide_frames=10,
    step_ms=10
)

RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(train_features_dir),
    sample_generator=train_spec_gen.spectrogram_generator(split='train', repeat=2),
    batch_size=100,
    verbose=True
)
os.sync()
time.sleep(1)

# Generate VALIDATION features (no augmentation) - 10% of data
print("\nGenerating VALIDATION features (10% of data, no augmentation)...")
val_clips = Clips(
    input_directory=str(training_dir),
    file_pattern='*.wav',
    max_clip_duration_s=None,
    remove_silence=False,
    random_split_seed=42,
    split_count=0.2
)
# Take half of the validation split for actual validation
val_indices = list(range(len(val_clips.split_clips['validation'])))
val_half = len(val_indices) // 2
print(f"  Validation split: {val_half} clips (half of held-out)")

val_spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration(
    clips=val_clips,
    augmenter=None,
    slide_frames=1,
    step_ms=10
)

# Generate only first half for validation
val_generator = val_spec_gen.spectrogram_generator(split='validation', repeat=1)
val_spectrograms = []
for i, spec in enumerate(val_generator):
    if i >= val_half:
        break
    val_spectrograms.append(spec)

if val_spectrograms:
    RaggedMmap.from_generator(
        out_dir=str(val_features_dir),
        sample_generator=iter(val_spectrograms),
        batch_size=100,
        verbose=True
    )
os.sync()
time.sleep(1)

# Generate TESTING features (no augmentation) - 10% of data
print("\nGenerating TESTING features (10% of data, no augmentation)...")
test_clips = Clips(
    input_directory=str(training_dir),
    file_pattern='*.wav',
    max_clip_duration_s=None,
    remove_silence=False,
    random_split_seed=42,
    split_count=0.2
)
print(f"  Testing split: {len(test_clips.split_clips['validation']) - val_half} clips (other half of held-out)")

test_spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration(
    clips=test_clips,
    augmenter=None,
    slide_frames=1,
    step_ms=10
)

# Generate second half for testing
test_generator = test_spec_gen.spectrogram_generator(split='validation', repeat=1)
test_spectrograms = []
for i, spec in enumerate(test_generator):
    if i < val_half:
        continue  # Skip first half (used for validation)
    test_spectrograms.append(spec)

if test_spectrograms:
    RaggedMmap.from_generator(
        out_dir=str(test_features_dir),
        sample_generator=iter(test_spectrograms),
        batch_size=100,
        verbose=True
    )
os.sync()
time.sleep(2)

# Verify output
print("\n" + "="*50)
print("Verifying generated features...")
try:
    train_mmap = RaggedMmap(str(train_features_dir), mode='r')
    val_mmap = RaggedMmap(str(val_features_dir), mode='r')
    test_mmap = RaggedMmap(str(test_features_dir), mode='r')
    print(f"  Train features:    {len(train_mmap):,} spectrograms")
    print(f"  Validation features: {len(val_mmap):,} spectrograms")
    print(f"  Testing features:    {len(test_mmap):,} spectrograms")
    if len(train_mmap) > 0:
        sample = train_mmap[0]
        print(f"  Sample shape: {sample.shape}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"  ERROR verifying: {e}")
    import traceback
    traceback.print_exc()

print(f"\nDirectory structure:")
print(f"  {train_features_dir}")
print(f"  {val_features_dir}")
print(f"  {test_features_dir}")
print("\nDone!")</cell id="cell-16">

<cell id="cell-25"># Cell 17: Download model (VS Code remote compatible)
import anywidget
import traitlets
import os
import base64
import mimetypes

class FileDownloader(anywidget.AnyWidget):
    """Widget to download files when using Colab via VS Code remote."""
    file_path = traitlets.Unicode(help="Path to the file to download").tag(sync=True)
    button_text = traitlets.Unicode("Download File").tag(sync=True)

    _esm = """
    export function render({ model, el }) {
      let btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.classList.add("jupyter-widgets", "jupyter-button", "widget-button");
      btn.style.width = "100%";
      btn.innerText = "Waiting for Kernel...";
      btn.disabled = true;

      model.on("change:button_text", () => {
        if (!btn.disabled) btn.innerText = model.get("button_text");
      });

      btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
        const filePath = model.get("file_path");
        if (!filePath) { alert("No file path set!"); return; }
        const originalText = btn.innerText;
        btn.innerText = "Downloading...";
        btn.disabled = true;
        model.send({ type: "request_download" });
        setTimeout(() => { btn.innerText = originalText; btn.disabled = false; }, 5000);
      });

      el.appendChild(btn);

      model.on("msg:custom", (msg) => {
        if (msg.type === "connection_verified") {
          btn.disabled = false;
          btn.innerText = model.get("button_text");
        } else if (msg.type === "file_content") {
          const byteCharacters = atob(msg.content);
          const byteNumbers = new Array(byteCharacters.length);
          for (let i = 0; i < byteCharacters.length; i++) {
            byteNumbers[i] = byteCharacters.charCodeAt(i);
          }
          const blob = new Blob([new Uint8Array(byteNumbers)], { type: msg.mime_type });
          const url = window.URL.createObjectURL(blob);
          const a = document.createElement("a");
          a.href = url; a.download = msg.filename;
          document.body.appendChild(a); a.click();
          window.URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
          document.body.removeChild(a);
          btn.innerText = model.get("button_text");
          btn.disabled = false;
        } else if (msg.type === "error") {
          alert(`Error: ${msg.message}`);
          btn.innerText = model.get("button_text");
          btn.disabled = false;
        }
      });

      setTimeout(() => { model.send({ type: "check_connection" }); }, 500);
    }
    """

    def __init__(self, file_path=None, button_text="Download File", **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        if file_path: self.file_path = file_path
        self.button_text = button_text
        self.on_msg(self._handle_custom_msg)

    def _handle_custom_msg(self, msg, content):
        if msg.get("type") == "check_connection":
            self.send({"type": "connection_verified"})
        elif msg.get("type") == "request_download":
            self._process_download()

    def _process_download(self):
        if not self.file_path or not os.path.exists(self.file_path):
            self.send({"type": "error", "message": f"File not found: {self.file_path}"})
            return
        try:
            mime_type, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(self.file_path)
            if mime_type is None: mime_type = 'application/octet-stream'
            with open(self.file_path, "rb") as f:
                b64_content = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode("utf-8")
            self.send({"type": "file_content", "filename": os.path.basename(self.file_path),
                       "mime_type": mime_type, "content": b64_content})
        except Exception as e:
            self.send({"type": "error", "message": str(e)})

# Display download buttons
from IPython.display import display
print(f"Download {WAKE_WORD_ID}.tflite -> copy to SD:/models/\n")

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-9"># Cell 6: Generate full training dataset (4X SCALED - Piper + XTTS with ALL TED samples)
import subprocess
import shutil
import torch
import librosa
import soundfile as sf
import urllib.request

training_dir = GENERATED_DIR / 'training'

# Clean up existing samples for fresh batch
if training_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(training_dir)
training_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

#=============================================================================
# PART 1: Download ALL TED speaker samples (8 speakers × 10 samples = 80 total)
#=============================================================================
speaker_voices_dir = WORK_DIR / 'speaker_voices'
speaker_voices_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# All 8 speakers, each with 10 samples
TED_SPEAKERS = ['BillGates', 'DaphneKoller', 'FeiFeiLi', 'GeorgeTakei', 
                'JaneGoodall', 'SalmanKhan', 'StephenHawking', 'StephenWolfram']
SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER = 10

speaker_files = []
print(f"Downloading ALL TED speaker samples ({len(TED_SPEAKERS)} speakers × {SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER} samples = {len(TED_SPEAKERS) * SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER} total)...")

for speaker in TED_SPEAKERS:
    for sample_idx in range(SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER):
        url = f'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/audio-samples/audio-samples.github.io/master/samples/mp3/ted_speakers/{speaker}/sample-{sample_idx}.mp3'
        mp3_path = speaker_voices_dir / f'ted_{speaker}_{sample_idx}.mp3'
        wav_path = speaker_voices_dir / f'ted_{speaker}_{sample_idx}.wav'
        
        if not wav_path.exists():
            try:
                urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, mp3_path)
                audio, sr = librosa.load(mp3_path, sr=16000, mono=True)
                if len(audio) > 6 * 16000:
                    audio = audio[:6 * 16000]  # 6 seconds for XTTS
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio, 16000)
                mp3_path.unlink()
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  ✗ {speaker}/sample-{sample_idx}: {e}")
                continue
        speaker_files.append(str(wav_path))
    print(f"  ✓ {speaker} ({SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER} samples)")

print(f"  Total: {len(speaker_files)} voice references\n")

#=============================================================================
# PART 2: Initialize XTTS-v2
#=============================================================================
print("Loading XTTS-v2 model...")
from TTS.api import TTS
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
xtts = TTS("tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2").to(device)
print(f"  XTTS-v2 loaded on {device}\n")

#=============================================================================
# PART 3: Generate samples with BOTH TTS engines
#=============================================================================
PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR = 100   # Piper: fast, diverse synthetic voices

# XTTS: Use subset of speakers per variation (randomly sample to avoid 1600 XTTS samples)
XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR = 20    # Use 20 random voice refs per variation

import random
random.seed(42)

total_piper = len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR
total_xtts = len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR
total_samples = total_piper + total_xtts

print(f"Generating {total_samples} samples:")
print(f"  Piper: {total_piper} samples ({PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR}/variation)")
print(f"  XTTS:  {total_xtts} samples ({XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR} voices/variation from {len(speaker_files)} available)")
print()

# --- PIPER GENERATION ---
print("PIPER TTS generation...")
for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}'")
    temp_dir = GENERATED_DIR / f'temp_piper_{i}'
    temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    subprocess.run([
        'python3', 'piper-sample-generator/generate_samples.py',
        variation,
        '--max-samples', str(PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR),
        '--batch-size', '10',
        '--output-dir', str(temp_dir),
        '--model', 'piper-sample-generator/models/en_US-libritts_r-medium.pt'
    ], capture_output=True)
    
    for wav in temp_dir.glob('*.wav'):
        new_name = f"piper_var{i}_{wav.name}"
        shutil.move(str(wav), str(training_dir / new_name))
    temp_dir.rmdir()

# --- XTTS GENERATION ---
print("\nXTTS-v2 generation (human-like voices from 80 TED samples)...")
for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    # Randomly sample voices for this variation
    selected_voices = random.sample(speaker_files, XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR)
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}' ({len(selected_voices)} voices)")
    
    for j, speaker_wav in enumerate(selected_voices):
        speaker_name = Path(speaker_wav).stem
        filename = training_dir / f"xtts_var{i}_{speaker_name}.wav"
        try:
            xtts.tts_to_file(
                text=variation,
                file_path=str(filename),
                speaker_wav=speaker_wav,
                language="en"
            )
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"    ✗ {speaker_name}: {e}")

sample_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))
print(f"\n✓ Generated {sample_count} total samples")
print(f"  Piper (synthetic): ~{total_piper}")
print(f"  XTTS (human-like): ~{total_xtts} (from {len(speaker_files)} voice references)")</cell id="cell-9">

<cell id="cell-12"># Cell 8: Download background noise audio
# AudioSet was converted to parquet - use datasets library
!pip install -q datasets soundfile

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

AUDIOSET_DIR = AUGMENTATION_DIR / 'audioset'
AUDIOSET_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Check if we already have audio files
existing = list(AUDIOSET_DIR.glob('*.wav'))
if len(existing) >= 100:
    print(f"AudioSet already has {len(existing)} samples, skipping download")
else:
    try:
        from datasets import load_dataset
        import soundfile as sf
        print("Loading AudioSet subset via datasets library...")
        
        # Load balanced subset with streaming
        ds = load_dataset(
            "agkphysics/AudioSet", 
            split="train",
            streaming=True,
            trust_remote_code=True
        )
        
        # Save first 500 audio samples as wav files
        count = 0
        max_samples = 500
        
        for sample in ds:
            if count >= max_samples:
                break
            try:
                audio = sample['audio']
                wav_path = AUDIOSET_DIR / f"audioset_{count:04d}.wav"
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio['array'], audio['sampling_rate'])
                count += 1
                if count % 100 == 0:
                    print(f"  Saved {count}/{max_samples} samples")
            except Exception:
                continue  # Skip problematic samples
        
        print(f"Done! Saved {count} background audio samples")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"AudioSet loading failed: {e}")
        print("Background augmentation will use MIT impulse responses only.")</cell id="cell-12">
<cell id="cell-13"># Cell 9: Download pre-computed negative features from HuggingFace
import zipfile

<cell id="cell-16"># Cell 11: Generate spectrogram features (with TESTING set)
from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips
from microwakeword.audio.spectrograms import SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja import RaggedMmap
import shutil
import os
import time

# Structure expected by microwakeword:
# features_dir/training/*_mmap/
# features_dir/validation/*_mmap/
# features_dir/testing/*_mmap/
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Create proper directory structure with _mmap suffix
train_base_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'training'
val_base_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'validation'
test_base_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'testing'
train_features_dir = train_base_dir / 'positive_mmap'
val_features_dir = val_base_dir / 'positive_mmap'
test_features_dir = test_base_dir / 'positive_mmap'

# Verify audio files exist
wav_files = list(training_dir.glob('*.wav'))
print(f"Found {len(wav_files)} wav files in {training_dir}")

# Clean up old features COMPLETELY
for d in [train_base_dir, val_base_dir, test_base_dir]:
    if d.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(d)
        print(f"  Deleted: {d}")
os.sync()
time.sleep(1)

# Create directories
for d in [train_features_dir, val_features_dir, test_features_dir]:
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

#=============================================================================
# Split: 80% train, 10% validation, 10% test
# We'll use two Clips objects with different seeds to create the splits
#=============================================================================

# Generate TRAINING features (with augmentation) - 80% of data
print("\nGenerating TRAINING features (80% of data, with augmentation)...")
train_clips = Clips(
    input_directory=str(training_dir),
    file_pattern='*.wav',
    max_clip_duration_s=None,
    remove_silence=False,
    random_split_seed=42,
    split_count=0.2  # 20% held out (will be split into val + test)
)
print(f"  Train split: {len(train_clips.split_clips['train'])} clips")

train_spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration(
    clips=train_clips,
    augmenter=augmentation,
    slide_frames=10,
    step_ms=10
)

RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(train_features_dir),
    sample_generator=train_spec_gen.spectrogram_generator(split='train', repeat=2),
    batch_size=100,
    verbose=True
)
os.sync()
time.sleep(1)

# Generate VALIDATION features (no augmentation) - 10% of data
print("\nGenerating VALIDATION features (10% of data, no augmentation)...")
val_clips = Clips(
    input_directory=str(training_dir),
    file_pattern='*.wav',
    max_clip_duration_s=None,
    remove_silence=False,
    random_split_seed=42,
    split_count=0.2
)
# Take half of the validation split for actual validation
val_indices = list(range(len(val_clips.split_clips['validation'])))
val_half = len(val_indices) // 2
print(f"  Validation split: {val_half} clips (half of held-out)")

val_spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration(
    clips=val_clips,
    augmenter=None,
    slide_frames=1,
    step_ms=10
)

# Generate only first half for validation
val_generator = val_spec_gen.spectrogram_generator(split='validation', repeat=1)
val_spectrograms = []
for i, spec in enumerate(val_generator):
    if i >= val_half:
        break
    val_spectrograms.append(spec)

if val_spectrograms:
    RaggedMmap.from_generator(
        out_dir=str(val_features_dir),
        sample_generator=iter(val_spectrograms),
        batch_size=100,
        verbose=True
    )
os.sync()
time.sleep(1)

# Generate TESTING features (no augmentation) - 10% of data
print("\nGenerating TESTING features (10% of data, no augmentation)...")
test_clips = Clips(
    input_directory=str(training_dir),
    file_pattern='*.wav',
    max_clip_duration_s=None,
    remove_silence=False,
    random_split_seed=42,
    split_count=0.2
)
print(f"  Testing split: {len(test_clips.split_clips['validation']) - val_half} clips (other half of held-out)")

test_spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration(
    clips=test_clips,
    augmenter=None,
    slide_frames=1,
    step_ms=10
)

# Generate second half for testing
test_generator = test_spec_gen.spectrogram_generator(split='validation', repeat=1)
test_spectrograms = []
for i, spec in enumerate(test_generator):
    if i < val_half:
        continue  # Skip first half (used for validation)
    test_spectrograms.append(spec)

if test_spectrograms:
    RaggedMmap.from_generator(
        out_dir=str(test_features_dir),
        sample_generator=iter(test_spectrograms),
        batch_size=100,
        verbose=True
    )
os.sync()
time.sleep(2)

# Verify output
print("\n" + "="*50)
print("Verifying generated features...")
try:
    train_mmap = RaggedMmap(str(train_features_dir), mode='r')
    val_mmap = RaggedMmap(str(val_features_dir), mode='r')
    test_mmap = RaggedMmap(str(test_features_dir), mode='r')
    print(f"  Train features:    {len(train_mmap):,} spectrograms")
    print(f"  Validation features: {len(val_mmap):,} spectrograms")
    print(f"  Testing features:    {len(test_mmap):,} spectrograms")
    if len(train_mmap) > 0:
        sample = train_mmap[0]
        print(f"  Sample shape: {sample.shape}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"  ERROR verifying: {e}")
    import traceback
    traceback.print_exc()

print(f"\nDirectory structure:")
print(f"  {train_features_dir}")
print(f"  {val_features_dir}")
print(f"  {test_features_dir}")
print("\nDone!")</cell id="cell-16">

<cell id="cell-25"># Cell 17: Download model (VS Code remote compatible)
import anywidget
import traitlets
import os
import base64
import mimetypes

class FileDownloader(anywidget.AnyWidget):
    """Widget to download files when using Colab via VS Code remote."""
    file_path = traitlets.Unicode(help="Path to the file to download").tag(sync=True)
    button_text = traitlets.Unicode("Download File").tag(sync=True)

    _esm = """
    export function render({ model, el }) {
      let btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.classList.add("jupyter-widgets", "jupyter-button", "widget-button");
      btn.style.width = "100%";
      btn.innerText = "Waiting for Kernel...";
      btn.disabled = true;

      model.on("change:button_text", () => {
        if (!btn.disabled) btn.innerText = model.get("button_text");
      });

      btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
        const filePath = model.get("file_path");
        if (!filePath) { alert("No file path set!"); return; }
        const originalText = btn.innerText;
        btn.innerText = "Downloading...";
        btn.disabled = true;
        model.send({ type: "request_download" });
        setTimeout(() => { btn.innerText = originalText; btn.disabled = false; }, 5000);
      });

      el.appendChild(btn);

      model.on("msg:custom", (msg) => {
        if (msg.type === "connection_verified") {
          btn.disabled = false;
          btn.innerText = model.get("button_text");
        } else if (msg.type === "file_content") {
          const byteCharacters = atob(msg.content);
          const byteNumbers = new Array(byteCharacters.length);
          for (let i = 0; i < byteCharacters.length; i++) {
            byteNumbers[i] = byteCharacters.charCodeAt(i);
          }
          const blob = new Blob([new Uint8Array(byteNumbers)], { type: msg.mime_type });
          const url = window.URL.createObjectURL(blob);
          const a = document.createElement("a");
          a.href = url; a.download = msg.filename;
          document.body.appendChild(a); a.click();
          window.URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
          document.body.removeChild(a);
          btn.innerText = model.get("button_text");
          btn.disabled = false;
        } else if (msg.type === "error") {
          alert(`Error: ${msg.message}`);
          btn.innerText = model.get("button_text");
          btn.disabled = false;
        }
      });

      setTimeout(() => { model.send({ type: "check_connection" }); }, 500);
    }
    """

    def __init__(self, file_path=None, button_text="Download File", **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        if file_path: self.file_path = file_path
        self.button_text = button_text
        self.on_msg(self._handle_custom_msg)

    def _handle_custom_msg(self, msg, content):
        if msg.get("type") == "check_connection":
            self.send({"type": "connection_verified"})
        elif msg.get("type") == "request_download":
            self._process_download()

    def _process_download(self):
        if not self.file_path or not os.path.exists(self.file_path):
            self.send({"type": "error", "message": f"File not found: {self.file_path}"})
            return
        try:
            mime_type, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(self.file_path)
            if mime_type is None: mime_type = 'application/octet-stream'
            with open(self.file_path, "rb") as f:
                b64_content = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode("utf-8")
            self.send({"type": "file_content", "filename": os.path.basename(self.file_path),
                       "mime_type": mime_type, "content": b64_content})
        except Exception as e:
            self.send({"type": "error", "message": str(e)})

# Display download buttons
from IPython.display import display
print(f"Download {WAKE_WORD_ID}.tflite -> copy to SD:/models/\n")

    selected_voices = random.sample(speaker_files, XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR)
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}' ({len(selected_voices)} voices)")
    
    for j, speaker_wav in enumerate(selected_voices):
        speaker_name = Path(speaker_wav).stem
        filename = training_dir / f"xtts_var{i}_{speaker_name}.wav"
        try:
            xtts.tts_to_file(
                text=variation,
                file_path=str(filename),
                speaker_wav=speaker_wav,
                language="en"
            )
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"    ✗ {speaker_name}: {e}")

sample_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))
print(f"\n✓ Generated {sample_count} total samples")
print(f"  Piper (synthetic): ~{total_piper}")
print(f"  XTTS (human-like): ~{total_xtts} (from {len(speaker_files)} voice references)")
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-5-20251101)**_

Good question! It was primarily a **time trade-off**, not an overfitting concern.

**The math:**
- XTTS is slow: ~3-5 seconds per sample (GPU) vs Piper's ~0.1 seconds
- Full XTTS: 80 voices × 20 variations = 1,600 samples → **~90-120 minutes** just for XTTS
- Current: 20 voices × 20 variations = 400 samples → **~20-30 minutes** for XTTS

**You're right that more XTTS would be better:**
- Human-like voices generalize better to real speech
- Augmentation (reverb, noise, pitch shift) multiplies each sample's value
- More diversity = less overfitting risk, not more

**If you want to max out XTTS**, you could set:
```python
XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR = 80  # Use ALL voice refs per variation
```

That would give you 1,600 XTTS samples + 2,000 Piper = **3,600 total** before augmentation. The feature generation does 2x augmented repeats, so you'd end up with ~7,200 training spectrograms from positive samples alone.

The main cost is generation time. If you have patience (or leave it running overnight), more XTTS = better model. The 8 TED speakers are genuinely diverse (male/female, different accents, speaking styles), so each additional sample adds real value.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-5-20251101)**_

Actually, the concern is the **opposite** - the negative datasets are *massive* compared to our positive data.

**The pre-computed negatives from HuggingFace:**
- `speech/` - hundreds of thousands of spectrograms (general speech)
- `dinner_party/` - similar scale (conversational audio)
- `no_speech/` - environmental sounds

Even with 3,600 positive samples × 2 augmentation repeats = ~7,200 positive spectrograms, the negatives likely have **500,000+** spectrograms combined.

**The training config handles this via:**
```python
'positive_class_weight': [1],
'negative_class_weight': [20],      # Negatives weighted 20x less in loss

# Sampling weights (how often each is sampled per batch)
'sampling_weight': 2.0   # positive
'sampling_weight': 10.0  # speech negative  
'sampling_weight': 10.0  # dinner party
'sampling_weight': 5.0   # no speech
```

**Why this imbalance is intentional:**
- Wake word detection should say "no" 99.9% of the time in real use
- The model needs to learn *lots* of ways speech can sound similar but not be "Hey Daisy"
- More negative diversity = fewer false positives

So you're fine - the negative data already dwarfs the positive, and the class weights + sampling weights balance the actual training batches. If anything, more positive data helps the model learn the wake word better without hurting false positive rejection.

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-9"># Cell 7: Generate full training dataset (4X SCALED - Piper + XTTS with ALL TED samples)
import subprocess
import shutil
import torch
import librosa
import soundfile as sf
import urllib.request

training_dir = GENERATED_DIR / 'training'

# Clean up existing samples for fresh batch
if training_dir.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(training_dir)
training_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

#=============================================================================
# PART 1: Download ALL TED speaker samples (8 speakers × 10 samples = 80 total)
#=============================================================================
speaker_voices_dir = WORK_DIR / 'speaker_voices'
speaker_voices_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# All 8 speakers, each with 10 samples
TED_SPEAKERS = ['BillGates', 'DaphneKoller', 'FeiFeiLi', 'GeorgeTakei', 
                'JaneGoodall', 'SalmanKhan', 'StephenHawking', 'StephenWolfram']
SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER = 10

speaker_files = []
print(f"Downloading ALL TED speaker samples ({len(TED_SPEAKERS)} speakers × {SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER} samples = {len(TED_SPEAKERS) * SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER} total)...")

for speaker in TED_SPEAKERS:
    for sample_idx in range(SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER):
        url = f'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/audio-samples/audio-samples.github.io/master/samples/mp3/ted_speakers/{speaker}/sample-{sample_idx}.mp3'
        mp3_path = speaker_voices_dir / f'ted_{speaker}_{sample_idx}.mp3'
        wav_path = speaker_voices_dir / f'ted_{speaker}_{sample_idx}.wav'
        
        if not wav_path.exists():
            try:
                urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, mp3_path)
                audio, sr = librosa.load(mp3_path, sr=16000, mono=True)
                if len(audio) > 6 * 16000:
                    audio = audio[:6 * 16000]  # 6 seconds for XTTS
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio, 16000)
                mp3_path.unlink()
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  ✗ {speaker}/sample-{sample_idx}: {e}")
                continue
        speaker_files.append(str(wav_path))
    print(f"  ✓ {speaker} ({SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER} samples)")

print(f"  Total: {len(speaker_files)} voice references\n")

#=============================================================================
# PART 2: Initialize XTTS-v2 (reuse from preview if available)
#=============================================================================
print("Loading XTTS-v2 model...")
from TTS.api import TTS
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
try:
    xtts = xtts_preview  # Reuse from Cell 6 preview
    print(f"  Reusing XTTS-v2 from preview cell")
except NameError:
    xtts = TTS("tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2").to(device)
    print(f"  XTTS-v2 loaded on {device}")
print()

#=============================================================================
# PART 3: Generate samples with BOTH TTS engines
#=============================================================================
PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR = 100   # Piper: fast, diverse synthetic voices

# XTTS: Use subset of speakers per variation (randomly sample to avoid 1600 XTTS samples)
XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR = 80    # Use 20 random voice refs per variation OR 80 for full set

import random
random.seed(42)

total_piper = len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR
total_xtts = len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR
total_samples = total_piper + total_xtts

print(f"Generating {total_samples} samples:")
print(f"  Piper: {total_piper} samples ({PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR}/variation)")
print(f"  XTTS:  {total_xtts} samples ({XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR} voices/variation from {len(speaker_files)} available)")
print()

# --- PIPER GENERATION ---
print("PIPER TTS generation...")
for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}'")
    temp_dir = GENERATED_DIR / f'temp_piper_{i}'
    temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    subprocess.run([
        'python3', 'piper-sample-generator/generate_samples.py',
        variation,
        '--max-samples', str(PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR),
        '--batch-size', '10',
        '--output-dir', str(temp_dir),
        '--model', 'piper-sample-generator/models/en_US-libritts_r-medium.pt'
    ], capture_output=True)
    
    for wav in temp_dir.glob('*.wav'):
        new_name = f"piper_var{i}_{wav.name}"
        shutil.move(str(wav), str(training_dir / new_name))
    temp_dir.rmdir()

# --- XTTS GENERATION ---
print("\nXTTS-v2 generation (human-like voices from 80 TED samples)...")
for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    # Randomly sample voices for this variation
    selected_voices = random.sample(speaker_files, XTTS_SPEAKERS_PER_VAR)
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}' ({len(selected_voices)} voices)")
    
    for j, speaker_wav in enumerate(selected_voices):
        speaker_name = Path(speaker_wav).stem
        filename = training_dir / f"xtts_var{i}_{speaker_name}.wav"
        try:
            xtts.tts_to_file(
                text=variation,
                file_path=str(filename),
                speaker_wav=speaker_wav,
                language="en"
            )
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"    ✗ {speaker_name}: {e}")

sample_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))
print(f"\n✓ Generated {sample_count} total samples")
print(f"  Piper (synthetic): ~{total_piper}")
print(f"  XTTS (human-like): ~{total_xtts} (from {len(speaker_files)} voice references)")</cell id="cell-9">

# AudioSet was converted to parquet - use datasets library
!pip install -q datasets soundfile

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

AUDIOSET_DIR = AUGMENTATION_DIR / 'audioset'
AUDIOSET_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Check if we already have audio files
existing = list(AUDIOSET_DIR.glob('*.wav'))
if len(existing) >= 100:
    print(f"AudioSet already has {len(existing)} samples, skipping download")
else:
    try:
        from datasets import load_dataset
        import soundfile as sf
        print("Loading AudioSet subset via datasets library...")
        
        # Load balanced subset with streaming
        ds = load_dataset(
            "agkphysics/AudioSet", 
            split="train",
            streaming=True,
            trust_remote_code=True
        )
        
        # Save first 500 audio samples as wav files
        count = 0
        max_samples = 500
        
        for sample in ds:
            if count >= max_samples:
                break
            try:
                audio = sample['audio']
                wav_path = AUDIOSET_DIR / f"audioset_{count:04d}.wav"
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio['array'], audio['sampling_rate'])
                count += 1
                if count % 100 == 0:
                    print(f"  Saved {count}/{max_samples} samples")
            except Exception:
                continue  # Skip problematic samples
        
        print(f"Done! Saved {count} background audio samples")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"AudioSet loading failed: {e}")
        print("Background augmentation will use MIT impulse responses only.")</cell id="cell-12">

<cell id="cell-16"># Cell 11: Generate spectrogram features (with TESTING set)
from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips
from microwakeword.audio.spectrograms import SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja import RaggedMmap
import shutil
import os
import time

# Structure expected by microwakeword:
# features_dir/training/*_mmap/
# features_dir/validation/*_mmap/
# features_dir/testing/*_mmap/
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'
POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Create proper directory structure with _mmap suffix
train_base_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'training'
val_base_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'validation'
test_base_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'testing'
train_features_dir = train_base_dir / 'positive_mmap'
val_features_dir = val_base_dir / 'positive_mmap'
test_features_dir = test_base_dir / 'positive_mmap'

# Verify audio files exist
wav_files = list(training_dir.glob('*.wav'))
print(f"Found {len(wav_files)} wav files in {training_dir}")

# Clean up old features COMPLETELY
for d in [train_base_dir, val_base_dir, test_base_dir]:
    if d.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(d)
        print(f"  Deleted: {d}")
os.sync()
time.sleep(1)

# Create directories
for d in [train_features_dir, val_features_dir, test_features_dir]:
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

#=============================================================================
# Split: 80% train, 10% validation, 10% test
# We'll use two Clips objects with different seeds to create the splits
#=============================================================================

# Generate TRAINING features (with augmentation) - 80% of data
print("\nGenerating TRAINING features (80% of data, with augmentation)...")
train_clips = Clips(
    input_directory=str(training_dir),
    file_pattern='*.wav',
    max_clip_duration_s=None,
    remove_silence=False,
    random_split_seed=42,
    split_count=0.2  # 20% held out (will be split into val + test)
)
print(f"  Train split: {len(train_clips.split_clips['train'])} clips")

train_spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration(
    clips=train_clips,
    augmenter=augmentation,
    slide_frames=10,
    step_ms=10
)

RaggedMmap.from_generator(
    out_dir=str(train_features_dir),
    sample_generator=train_spec_gen.spectrogram_generator(split='train', repeat=2),
    batch_size=100,
    verbose=True
)
os.sync()
time.sleep(1)

# Generate VALIDATION features (no augmentation) - 10% of data
print("\nGenerating VALIDATION features (10% of data, no augmentation)...")
val_clips = Clips(
    input_directory=str(training_dir),
    file_pattern='*.wav',
    max_clip_duration_s=None,
    remove_silence=False,
    random_split_seed=42,
    split_count=0.2
)
# Take half of the validation split for actual validation
val_indices = list(range(len(val_clips.split_clips['validation'])))
val_half = len(val_indices) // 2
print(f"  Validation split: {val_half} clips (half of held-out)")

val_spec_gen = SpectrogramGeneration(
    clips=val_clips,
    augmenter=None,
    slide_frames=1,
    step_ms=10
)

# Generate only first half for validation
val_generator = val_spec_gen.spectrogram_generator(split='validation', repeat=1)
val_spectrograms = []

<cell id="cell-25"># Cell 17: Download model (VS Code remote compatible)
import anywidget
import traitlets
import os
import base64
import mimetypes

class FileDownloader(anywidget.AnyWidget):
    """Widget to download files when using Colab via VS Code remote."""
    file_path = traitlets.Unicode(help="Path to the file to download").tag(sync=True)
    button_text = traitlets.Unicode("Download File").tag(sync=True)

    _esm = """
    export function render({ model, el }) {
      let btn = document.createElement("button");
      btn.classList.add("jupyter-widgets", "jupyter-button", "widget-button");
      btn.style.width = "100%";
      btn.innerText = "Waiting for Kernel...";
      btn.disabled = true;

      model.on("change:button_text", () => {
        if (!btn.disabled) btn.innerText = model.get("button_text");
      });

      btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
        const filePath = model.get("file_path");
        if (!filePath) { alert("No file path set!"); return; }
        const originalText = btn.innerText;
        btn.innerText = "Downloading...";
        btn.disabled = true;
        model.send({ type: "request_download" });
        setTimeout(() => { btn.innerText = originalText; btn.disabled = false; }, 5000);
      });

      el.appendChild(btn);

      model.on("msg:custom", (msg) => {
        if (msg.type === "connection_verified") {
          btn.disabled = false;
          btn.innerText = model.get("button_text");
        } else if (msg.type === "file_content") {
          const byteCharacters = atob(msg.content);
          const byteNumbers = new Array(byteCharacters.length);
          for (let i = 0; i < byteCharacters.length; i++) {
            byteNumbers[i] = byteCharacters.charCodeAt(i);
          }
          const blob = new Blob([new Uint8Array(byteNumbers)], { type: msg.mime_type });
          const url = window.URL.createObjectURL(blob);
          const a = document.createElement("a");
          a.href = url; a.download = msg.filename;
          document.body.appendChild(a); a.click();
          window.URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
          document.body.removeChild(a);
          btn.innerText = model.get("button_text");
          btn.disabled = false;
        } else if (msg.type === "error") {
          alert(`Error: ${msg.message}`);
          btn.innerText = model.get("button_text");
          btn.disabled = false;
        }
      });

      setTimeout(() => { model.send({ type: "check_connection" }); }, 500);
    }
    """

    def __init__(self, file_path=None, button_text="Download File", **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        if file_path: self.file_path = file_path
        self.button_text = button_text
        self.on_msg(self._handle_custom_msg)

    def _handle_custom_msg(self, msg, content):
        if msg.get("type") == "check_connection":
            self.send({"type": "connection_verified"})
        elif msg.get("type") == "request_download":
            self._process_download()

    def _process_download(self):
        if not self.file_path or not os.path.exists(self.file_path):
            self.send({"type": "error", "message": f"File not found: {self.file_path}"})
            return
        try:
            mime_type, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(self.file_path)
            if mime_type is None: mime_type = 'application/octet-stream'
            with open(self.file_path, "rb") as f:
                b64_content = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode("utf-8")
            self.send({"type": "file_content", "filename": os.path.basename(self.file_path),
                       "mime_type": mime_type, "content": b64_content})
        except Exception as e:
            self.send({"type": "error", "message": str(e)})

# Display download buttons

The challenge is:

                if len(audio) > 6 * 16000:
                    audio = audio[:6 * 16000]
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio, 16000)

                'JaneGoodall', 'SalmanKhan', 'StephenHawking', 'StephenWolfram']
SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER = 10
PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR = 100

total_voices = len(TED_SPEAKERS) * SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER  # 80
total_piper = len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * PIPER_SAMPLES_PER_VAR
total_xtts = len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * total_voices

print(f"Target: {total_piper + total_xtts} samples")

print()

for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS)}] '{variation}'")
    temp_dir = GENERATED_DIR / f'temp_piper_{i}'
    temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    
    subprocess.run([
        'python3', 'piper-sample-generator/generate_samples.py',

    ], capture_output=True)
    
    for wav in temp_dir.glob('*.wav'):
        new_name = f"piper_var{i}_{wav.name}"
        shutil.move(str(wav), str(training_dir / new_name))
    shutil.rmtree(temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)

piper_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('piper_*.wav')))
print(f"\n✓ Piper complete: {piper_count} samples")
gc.collect()

#=============================================================================
# PHASE 2: DOWNLOAD TED SPEAKER SAMPLES
#=============================================================================
print("\n" + "="*60)
print("PHASE 2: DOWNLOAD TED SPEAKERS")
print("="*60)

import urllib.request
import librosa
import soundfile as sf

speaker_voices_dir = WORK_DIR / 'speaker_voices'
speaker_voices_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

speaker_files = []
for speaker in TED_SPEAKERS:
    for sample_idx in range(SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER):
        wav_path = speaker_voices_dir / f'ted_{speaker}_{sample_idx}.wav'
        mp3_path = speaker_voices_dir / f'ted_{speaker}_{sample_idx}.mp3'
        
        if not wav_path.exists():
            try:
                url = f'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/audio-samples/audio-samples.github.io/master/samples/mp3/ted_speakers/{speaker}/sample-{sample_idx}.mp3'
                urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, mp3_path)
                audio, sr = librosa.load(mp3_path, sr=16000, mono=True)
                if len(audio) > 6 * 16000:
                    audio = audio[:6 * 16000]
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio, 16000)
                mp3_path.unlink()
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  ✗ {speaker}/sample-{sample_idx}: {e}")
                continue
        speaker_files.append(str(wav_path))
    print(f"  ✓ {speaker} ({SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER} samples)")

print(f"\n✓ Downloaded {len(speaker_files)} voice references")

#=============================================================================
# PHASE 3: XTTS GENERATION (PARALLEL)
#=============================================================================
print("\n" + "="*60)
print(f"PHASE 3: XTTS-v2 ({NUM_XTTS_WORKERS} parallel workers)")
print("="*60)

# Build task list: (variation_idx, variation_text, speaker_wav, output_path)
xtts_tasks = []
for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
    for speaker_wav in speaker_files:
        speaker_name = Path(speaker_wav).stem
        output_path = str(training_dir / f"xtts_var{i}_{speaker_name}.wav")
        xtts_tasks.append((variation, speaker_wav, output_path))

print(f"  Total XTTS tasks: {len(xtts_tasks)}")

# Worker function - each process loads its own XTTS
def xtts_worker(task_batch):
    """Process a batch of XTTS tasks in a separate process."""
    import torch
    from TTS.api import TTS
    
    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    tts = TTS("tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2").to(device)
    
    results = []
    for variation, speaker_wav, output_path in task_batch:
        try:
            tts.tts_to_file(
                text=variation,
                file_path=output_path,
                speaker_wav=speaker_wav,
                language="en"
            )
            results.append((output_path, True))
        except Exception as e:
            results.append((output_path, False, str(e)))
    
    # Cleanup
    del tts
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    return results

# Split tasks into batches for each worker
def chunk_list(lst, n):
    chunk_size = len(lst) // n + (1 if len(lst) % n else 0)
    return [lst[i:i + chunk_size] for i in range(0, len(lst), chunk_size)]

if NUM_XTTS_WORKERS == 1:
    # Single worker - simpler, no multiprocessing overhead
    import torch
    from TTS.api import TTS
    
    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    xtts = TTS("tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2").to(device)
    print(f"  XTTS-v2 loaded on {device}")
    
    for idx, (variation, speaker_wav, output_path) in enumerate(xtts_tasks):
        if idx % 80 == 0:  # Progress every variation
            print(f"  Progress: {idx}/{len(xtts_tasks)} ({100*idx//len(xtts_tasks)}%)")
        try:
            xtts.tts_to_file(
                text=variation,
                file_path=output_path,
                speaker_wav=speaker_wav,
                language="en"
            )
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"    ✗ {Path(output_path).stem}: {e}")
    
    del xtts
    gc.collect()
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
else:
    # Multi-worker parallel processing
    task_batches = chunk_list(xtts_tasks, NUM_XTTS_WORKERS)
    print(f"  Split into {len(task_batches)} batches of ~{len(task_batches[0])} tasks each")
    
    # Use spawn to avoid CUDA fork issues
    mp.set_start_method('spawn', force=True)
    
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=NUM_XTTS_WORKERS) as executor:
        futures = {executor.submit(xtts_worker, batch): i for i, batch in enumerate(task_batches)}
        
        completed = 0
        for future in as_completed(futures):
            batch_idx = futures[future]
            try:
                results = future.result()
                success = sum(1 for r in results if r[1])
                completed += 1
                print(f"  Worker {batch_idx+1}/{NUM_XTTS_WORKERS} done: {success}/{len(results)} samples")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  Worker {batch_idx+1} failed: {e}")

xtts_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('xtts_*.wav')))
print(f"\n✓ XTTS complete: {xtts_count} samples")

gc.collect()

#=============================================================================
# SUMMARY
#=============================================================================
print("\n" + "="*60)
total_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))
print(f"✓ GENERATION COMPLETE: {total_count} total samples")
print(f"  Piper: {piper_count}")
print(f"  XTTS:  {xtts_count}")
print("="*60)
