   208→void loop() {
   209→  // Capture audio
   210→  if (!captureAudio()) {
   211→    return;
   212→  }
   213→
   214→  // Keep processing audio through frontend until it stops producing features
   215→  while (audio_buffer_pos >= FEATURE_STRIDE_SAMPLES) {
   216→    // Feed ALL available audio to frontend (it will consume what it needs)
   217→    size_t num_samples_read;
   218→    FrontendOutput frontend_output = FrontendProcessSamples(
   219→        &frontend_state, audio_buffer, audio_buffer_pos, &num_samples_read);
   220→
   221→    // If no samples consumed, we need more audio
   222→    if (num_samples_read == 0) {
   223→      break;
   224→    }
   225→
   226→    // Shift audio buffer by consumed samples
   227→    if (num_samples_read < audio_buffer_pos) {
   228→      memmove(audio_buffer, audio_buffer + num_samples_read,
   229→              (audio_buffer_pos - num_samples_read) * sizeof(int16_t));
   230→    }
   231→    audio_buffer_pos -= num_samples_read;
   232→
   233→    // If we got features, add to feature buffer
   234→    if (frontend_output.size == FEATURE_BINS) {
   235→      // Shift existing frames left and add new one at end
   236→      if (feature_frame_count >= FEATURE_FRAMES) {
   237→        memmove(feature_buffer, feature_buffer + FEATURE_BINS,
   238→                (FEATURE_FRAMES - 1) * FEATURE_BINS * sizeof(uint16_t));
   239→        feature_frame_count = FEATURE_FRAMES - 1;
   240→      }
   241→
   242→      // Copy new frame
   243→      memcpy(feature_buffer + feature_frame_count * FEATURE_BINS,
   244→             frontend_output.values, FEATURE_BINS * sizeof(uint16_t));
   245→      feature_frame_count++;
   246→
   247→      // Run inference when we have 3 frames
   248→      if (feature_frame_count >= FEATURE_FRAMES) {
   249→#if DEBUG_FEATURES
   250→        static int debug_count = 0;
   251→        if (++debug_count >= 30) {
   252→          debug_count = 0;
   253→          // Show raw feature values and energy
   254→          uint32_t energy = 0;
   255→          uint16_t max_feat = 0;
   256→          for (int i = 0; i < FEATURE_FRAMES * FEATURE_BINS; i++) {
   257→            energy += feature_buffer[i];
   258→            if (feature_buffer[i] > max_feat) max_feat = feature_buffer[i];
   259→          }
   260→          Serial.printf("Features: max=%u, sum=%lu\n", max_feat, energy);
   261→        }
   262→#endif
   263→        float prob = runInference();
   264→
   265→        if (detectWakeword(prob)) {
   266→          Serial.printf("\n>>> %s DETECTED! <<<\n\n", WAKE_WORD_NAME);
   267→          digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH);
   268→          delay(500);
   269→          digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW);
   270→
   271→          for (int i = 0; i < SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
   272→            probability_window[i] = 0.0f;
   273→          }
   274→          window_filled = false;
   275→        }
   276→      }
   277→    }
   278→  }
   279→}

   281→bool initInterpreter() {
   282→  // Get model
   283→  const tflite::Model* model = tflite::GetModel(model_data);
   284→  if (model->version() != TFLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION) {
   285→    Serial.printf("Model version mismatch: %d vs %d\n",
   286→                  model->version(), TFLITE_SCHEMA_VERSION);
   287→    return false;
   288→  }
   289→
   290→  // Create allocator for resource variables (streaming model state)
   291→  var_allocator = tflite::MicroAllocator::Create(var_arena, VAR_ARENA_SIZE);
   292→  if (!var_allocator) {
   293→    Serial.println("Failed to create var allocator");
   294→    return false;
   295→  }
   296→
   297→  // Create resource variables container
   298→  resource_vars = tflite::MicroResourceVariables::Create(var_allocator, MAX_RESOURCE_VARS);
   299→  if (!resource_vars) {
   300→    Serial.println("Failed to create resource variables");
   301→    return false;
   302→  }
   303→
   304→  // Create interpreter WITH resource variables support
   305→  static tflite::MicroInterpreter static_interpreter(
   306→      model, resolver, tensor_arena, TENSOR_ARENA_SIZE, resource_vars);
   307→  interpreter = &static_interpreter;
   308→
   309→  // Allocate tensors
   310→  if (interpreter->AllocateTensors() != kTfLiteOk) {
   311→    Serial.println("AllocateTensors failed");
   312→    return false;
   313→  }
   314→
   315→  // Get input/output tensors
   316→  input_tensor = interpreter->input(0);
   317→  output_tensor = interpreter->output(0);
   318→
   319→  if (!input_tensor || !output_tensor) {
   320→    Serial.println("Failed to get tensors");
   321→    return false;
   322→  }
   323→
   324→  return true;
   325→}

   397→bool captureAudio() {
   398→  // Only read if we have space in buffer
   399→  int space_available = AUDIO_BUFFER_SIZE - audio_buffer_pos;
   400→  if (space_available < 256) {
   401→    return true;  // Buffer has data, let it be processed first
   402→  }
   403→
   404→  // Read smaller chunks more frequently for smoother audio
   405→  int samples_to_read = min(256, space_available);
   406→  size_t bytes_read;
   407→  if (i2s_read(I2S_NUM_0, i2s_buffer, samples_to_read * 4, &bytes_read, 10) != ESP_OK) {
   408→    return false;
   409→  }
   410→
   411→  int samples = bytes_read / 4;
   412→
   413→  // Track audio levels for debug
   414→  static int audio_debug = 0;
   415→  int32_t max_sample = 0;
   416→
   417→  for (int i = 0; i < samples; i++) {
   418→    // Convert 32-bit I2S to 16-bit
   419→    // INMP441 outputs 24-bit in MSB of 32-bit word, shift right to get 16-bit
   420→    int32_t sample = i2s_buffer[i] >> 14;  // >>14 for moderate gain
   421→    audio_buffer[audio_buffer_pos++] = constrain(sample, -32768, 32767);
   422→
   423→    if (abs(sample) > max_sample) max_sample = abs(sample);
   424→  }
   425→
   426→#if DEBUG_FEATURES
   427→  if (++audio_debug >= 300) {
   428→    audio_debug = 0;
   429→    Serial.printf("Audio: amp=%ld, buf=%d\n", max_sample, audio_buffer_pos);
   430→  }
   431→#endif
   432→
   433→  return true;
   434→}

   436→float runInference() {
   437→  // Copy 3 frames of features to input tensor
   438→  int total_features = FEATURE_FRAMES * FEATURE_BINS;  // 3 * 40 = 120
   439→
   440→  // Debug: print quant params once
   441→  static bool printed_params = false;
   442→  if (!printed_params) {
   443→    printed_params = true;
   444→    Serial.printf("\n=== INFERENCE DEBUG ===\n");
   445→    Serial.printf("Input type=%d, scale=%.6f, zp=%d\n",
   446→      input_tensor->type, input_tensor->params.scale, input_tensor->params.zero_point);
   447→    Serial.printf("Output type=%d, scale=%.6f, zp=%d\n",
   448→      output_tensor->type, output_tensor->params.scale, output_tensor->params.zero_point);
   449→    Serial.printf("Input bytes=%d, Output bytes=%d\n",
   450→      input_tensor->bytes, output_tensor->bytes);
   451→  }
   452→
   453→  if (input_tensor->type == kTfLiteInt8) {
   454→    int8_t* input_data = input_tensor->data.int8;
   455→
   456→    // Use ESPHome's proven formula directly
   457→    for (int i = 0; i < total_features; i++) {
   458→      int32_t scaled = ((int32_t)feature_buffer[i] * 256 + 333) / 666 - 128;
   459→      input_data[i] = constrain(scaled, -128, 127);
   460→    }
   461→
   462→    // Debug: show first few input values once
   463→    static int input_debug = 0;
   464→    if (++input_debug == 50) {
   465→      Serial.printf("Input[0-5]: %d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d\n",
   466→        input_data[0], input_data[1], input_data[2],
   467→        input_data[3], input_data[4], input_data[5]);
   468→    }
   469→  } else {
   470→    // Float model
   471→    float* input_data = input_tensor->data.f;
   472→    for (int i = 0; i < total_features; i++) {
   473→      input_data[i] = feature_buffer[i] / 25.6f;
   474→    }
   475→  }
   476→
   477→  // Run inference
   478→  if (interpreter->Invoke() != kTfLiteOk) {
   479→    Serial.println("Invoke failed");
   480→    return 0.0f;
   481→  }
   482→
   483→  // Get output probability
   484→  float probability;
   485→
   486→  // Debug: show raw output once
   487→  static int out_debug = 0;
   488→
   489→  if (output_tensor->type == kTfLiteUInt8) {
   490→    uint8_t output_value = output_tensor->data.uint8[0];
   491→    probability = (output_value - output_tensor->params.zero_point) *
   492→                  output_tensor->params.scale;
   493→    if (++out_debug == 50) {
   494→      Serial.printf("Raw output uint8=%u, prob=%.4f\n", output_value, probability);
   495→    }
   496→  } else if (output_tensor->type == kTfLiteInt8) {
   497→    int8_t output_value = output_tensor->data.int8[0];
   498→    probability = (output_value - output_tensor->params.zero_point) *
   499→                  output_tensor->params.scale;
   500→    if (++out_debug == 50) {
   501→      Serial.printf("Raw output int8=%d, prob=%.4f\n", output_value, probability);
   502→    }
   503→  } else {
   504→    probability = output_tensor->data.f[0];
   505→    if (++out_debug == 50) {
   506→      Serial.printf("Raw output float=%.4f\n", probability);
   507→    }
   508→  }
   509→
   510→  return probability;
   511→}
   512→
   513→bool detectWakeword(float probability) {
   514→  // Add to sliding window
   515→  probability_window[window_pos] = probability;
   516→  window_pos = (window_pos + 1) % SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;
   517→
   518→  if (window_pos == 0) {
   519→    window_filled = true;
   520→  }
   521→
   522→  // Don't trigger until window is filled
   523→  if (!window_filled) {
   524→    return false;
   525→  }
   526→
   527→  // Calculate average probability
   528→  float avg = 0.0f;
   529→  for (int i = 0; i < SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
   530→    avg += probability_window[i];
   531→  }
   532→  avg /= SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;
   533→
   534→  // Log probability (always show for debugging)
   535→  static int log_count = 0;
   536→  if (probability > 0.01f || ++log_count >= 100) {
   537→    Serial.printf("prob: %.4f, avg: %.4f\n", probability, avg);
   538→    log_count = 0;
   539→  }
   540→
   541→  return avg >= PROBABILITY_CUTOFF;
   542→}

   546→    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
   547→    delay(200);
   548→  }
   549→}

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-4"># Patch microWakeWord for TensorFlow 2.17 compatibility
# TF 2.17 returns numpy arrays directly instead of tensors, so .numpy() calls fail

import re

train_py = '/workspace/microWakeWord/microwakeword/train.py'

with open(train_py, 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Check if already patched
if 'np.asarray' not in content:
    # Replace patterns like: result["fp"].numpy() -> np.asarray(result["fp"])
    # This handles both tensor (needs .numpy()) and numpy array (already is) cases
    patched = re.sub(
        r'(\w+)\[(["\'])(\w+)\2\]\.numpy\(\)',
        r'np.asarray(\1["\3"])',
        content
    )
    
    with open(train_py, 'w') as f:
        f.write(patched)
    
    print("✓ Patched train.py for TensorFlow 2.17 compatibility")
else:
    print("✓ train.py already patched")</cell id="cell-4">

✓ Patched train.py for TensorFlow 2.17 compatibility

speaker_voices_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

speaker_files = []
for speaker in TED_SPEAKERS:
    for sample_idx in range(SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER):
        wav_path = speaker_voices_dir / f'ted_{speaker}_{sample_idx}.wav'
        mp3_path = speaker_voices_dir / f'ted_{speaker}_{sample_idx}.mp3'
        
        if not wav_path.exists():
            try:
                url = f'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/audio-samples/audio-samples.github.io/master/samples/mp3/ted_speakers/{speaker}/sample-{sample_idx}.mp3'
                urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, mp3_path)
                audio, sr = librosa.load(mp3_path, sr=16000, mono=True)
                if len(audio) > 6 * 16000:
                    audio = audio[:6 * 16000]
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio, 16000)
                mp3_path.unlink()
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  ✗ {speaker}/sample-{sample_idx}: {e}")
                continue
        speaker_files.append(str(wav_path))
    print(f"  ✓ {speaker} ({SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER} samples)")

print(f"\n✓ Downloaded {len(speaker_files)} voice references")</cell id="cell-11">

# PHASE 3: XTTS GENERATION (SKIP IF DATA EXISTS)
#=============================================================================
if SKIP_GENERATION:
    print("✓ Skipping XTTS generation - using existing data")
else:
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("PHASE 3: XTTS-v2 GENERATION")
    print("="*60)

    import torch
    from TTS.api import TTS

    # Build task list: (variation_text, speaker_wav, output_path)
    xtts_tasks = []
    for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
        for speaker_wav in speaker_files:
            speaker_name = Path(speaker_wav).stem
            output_path = str(training_dir / f"xtts_var{i}_{speaker_name}.wav")
            # Skip if already generated (resume support)
            if not Path(output_path).exists():
                xtts_tasks.append((variation, speaker_wav, output_path))

    total_tasks = len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * len(speaker_files)
    already_done = total_tasks - len(xtts_tasks)

    print(f"  Total XTTS tasks: {total_tasks}")
    if already_done > 0:
        print(f"  Already completed: {already_done} (resuming...)")
    print(f"  Remaining: {len(xtts_tasks)}")

    if len(xtts_tasks) > 0:
        # Load XTTS model
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
        print(f"\n  Loading XTTS-v2 on {device}...")
        xtts = TTS("tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2").to(device)
        print("  Model loaded!")
        
        # Sequential generation with progress
        failed = 0
        for idx, (variation, speaker_wav, output_path) in enumerate(xtts_tasks):
            # Progress every 80 samples (1 variation * 80 voices)
            if idx % 80 == 0:
                pct = 100 * (idx + already_done) // total_tasks
                print(f"  Progress: {idx + already_done}/{total_tasks} ({pct}%)")
            
            try:
                xtts.tts_to_file(
                    text=variation,
                    file_path=output_path,
                    speaker_wav=speaker_wav,
                    language="en"
                )
            except Exception as e:
                failed += 1
                if failed <= 5:  # Only show first 5 errors
                    print(f"    ✗ {Path(output_path).stem}: {e}")
        
        # Cleanup
        del xtts
        gc.collect()
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        
        if failed > 0:
            print(f"\n  ⚠ {failed} samples failed")

    xtts_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('xtts_*.wav')))
    print(f"\n✓ XTTS complete: {xtts_count} samples")
    gc.collect()</cell id="cell-12">

from microwakeword.audio.augmentation import Augmentation

# Verify we have background noise files
audioset_files = list(AUDIOSET_DIR.glob('*.wav'))
if len(audioset_files) == 0:
    raise RuntimeError(f"No AudioSet files found in {AUDIOSET_DIR}! Re-run AudioSet download cell.")

augmentation = Augmentation(
    augmentation_duration_s=3.2,
    augmentation_probabilities={
        "SevenBandParametricEQ": 0.1,
        "TanhDistortion": 0.1,
        "PitchShift": 0.1,
        "BandStopFilter": 0.1,
        "AddColorNoise": 0.1,
        "AddBackgroundNoise": 0.75,
        "Gain": 1.0,
        "RIR": 0.5,
    },
    impulse_paths=[str(MIT_IR_DIR / 'Audio')],
    background_paths=[str(AUDIOSET_DIR)],
)
print(f"Augmentation configured with {len(audioset_files)} background noise files")</cell id="cell-19">

<cell id="cell-20"># Cell 11: Generate spectrogram features from audio samples
from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips
from microwakeword.audio.spectrograms import SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja.ragged import RaggedMmap
import os

POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'

# Check if features already exist
train_mmap = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'training' / 'wakeword_mmap'
if train_mmap.exists():
    print("✓ Features already exist, skipping generation")
else:
    print("Generating spectrogram features from audio samples...")
    print(f"  Source: {training_dir} ({len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))} wav files)")
    print(f"  Output: {POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR}")
    print()
    
    # Create Clips object pointing to audio files
    clips = Clips(
        input_directory=str(training_dir),
        file_pattern='*.wav',
        max_clip_duration_s=None,
        remove_silence=False,
        random_split_seed=10,
        split_count=0.1,  # 10% for validation
    )
    
    # Create output directories
    POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    splits = ["training", "validation"]
    for split in splits:
        out_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / split
        out_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        
        split_name = "train" if split == "training" else "validation"
        repetition = 10 if split == "training" else 1  # More augmented copies for training
        
        spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(
            clips=clips,
            augmenter=augmentation,
            slide_frames=10,
            step_ms=10,
        )
        
        print(f"  Generating {split} features (repeat={repetition})...")
        RaggedMmap.from_generator(
            out_dir=str(out_dir / 'wakeword_mmap'),
            sample_generator=spectrograms.spectrogram_generator(
                split=split_name, 
                repeat=repetition
            ),
            batch_size=100,
            verbose=True,
        )
    
    print("\n✓ Feature generation complete")

# Verify
train_features = RaggedMmap(str(POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'training' / 'wakeword_mmap'), mode='r')
val_features = RaggedMmap(str(POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'validation' / 'wakeword_mmap'), mode='r')
print(f"  Training features: {len(train_features)} spectrograms")
print(f"  Validation features: {len(val_features)} spectrograms")</cell id="cell-20">

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-4"># Patch microWakeWord for TensorFlow 2.17 compatibility
# TF 2.17 returns numpy arrays directly instead of tensors, so .numpy() calls fail

import re

train_py = '/workspace/microWakeWord/microwakeword/train.py'

with open(train_py, 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Check if already patched
if 'np.asarray' not in content:
    # Replace patterns like: result["fp"].numpy() -> np.asarray(result["fp"])
    # This handles both tensor (needs .numpy()) and numpy array (already is) cases
    patched = re.sub(
        r'(\w+)\[(["\'])(\w+)\2\]\.numpy\(\)',
        r'np.asarray(\1["\3"])',
        content
    )
    
    with open(train_py, 'w') as f:
        f.write(patched)
    
    print("✓ Patched train.py for TensorFlow 2.17 compatibility")
else:
    print("✓ train.py already patched")</cell id="cell-4">

✓ Patched train.py for TensorFlow 2.17 compatibility

# PHASE 3: XTTS GENERATION (SKIP IF DATA EXISTS)

if SKIP_GENERATION:
    print("✓ Skipping XTTS generation - using existing data")
else:
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("PHASE 3: XTTS-v2 GENERATION")
    print("="*60)

    import torch
    from TTS.api import TTS

    # Build task list: (variation_text, speaker_wav, output_path)
    xtts_tasks = []
    for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
        for speaker_wav in speaker_files:
            speaker_name = Path(speaker_wav).stem
            output_path = str(training_dir / f"xtts_var{i}_{speaker_name}.wav")
            # Skip if already generated (resume support)
            if not Path(output_path).exists():
                xtts_tasks.append((variation, speaker_wav, output_path))

    total_tasks = len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * len(speaker_files)
    already_done = total_tasks - len(xtts_tasks)

    print(f"  Total XTTS tasks: {total_tasks}")
    if already_done > 0:
        print(f"  Already completed: {already_done} (resuming...)")
    print(f"  Remaining: {len(xtts_tasks)}")

    if len(xtts_tasks) > 0:
        # Load XTTS model
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
        print(f"\n  Loading XTTS-v2 on {device}...")
        xtts = TTS("tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2").to(device)
        print("  Model loaded!")
        
        # Sequential generation with progress
        failed = 0
        for idx, (variation, speaker_wav, output_path) in enumerate(xtts_tasks):
            # Progress every 80 samples (1 variation * 80 voices)
            if idx % 80 == 0:
                pct = 100 * (idx + already_done) // total_tasks
                print(f"  Progress: {idx + already_done}/{total_tasks} ({pct}%)")
            
            try:
                xtts.tts_to_file(
                    text=variation,
                    file_path=output_path,
                    speaker_wav=speaker_wav,
                    language="en"
                )
            except Exception as e:
                failed += 1
                if failed <= 5:  # Only show first 5 errors
                    print(f"    ✗ {Path(output_path).stem}: {e}")
        
        # Cleanup
        del xtts
        gc.collect()
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        
        if failed > 0:
            print(f"\n  ⚠ {failed} samples failed")

    xtts_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('xtts_*.wav')))
    print(f"\n✓ XTTS complete: {xtts_count} samples")
    gc.collect()</cell id="cell-12">

else:

<cell id="cell-16">#=============================================================================
# GENERATE CONFUSABLE NEGATIVES WITH PIPER TTS
#=============================================================================
if SKIP_CONFUSABLE_GEN:
    print("✓ Skipping confusable generation - using existing data")
else:
    print("="*60)
    print("GENERATING CONFUSABLE NEGATIVES (Piper TTS)")
    print("="*60)
    
    import subprocess
    import shutil
    
    for i, phrase in enumerate(CONFUSABLE_NEGATIVES):
        print(f"  [{i+1}/{len(CONFUSABLE_NEGATIVES)}] '{phrase.strip()}'")
        temp_dir = GENERATED_DIR / f'temp_confusable_{i}'
        temp_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        
        try:
            subprocess.run([
                'python3', 'piper-sample-generator/generate_samples.py',
                phrase,
                '--max-samples', str(CONFUSABLE_SAMPLES_PER_PHRASE),
                '--batch-size', '10',
                '--output-dir', str(temp_dir),
                '--model', 'piper-sample-generator/models/en_US-libritts_r-medium.pt'
            ], capture_output=True, timeout=120)
            
            # Move generated files
            for wav in temp_dir.glob('*.wav'):
                # Sanitize phrase for filename
                safe_phrase = phrase.strip().replace(' ', '_').replace('.', '')[:20]
                new_name = f"confusable_{i}_{safe_phrase}_{wav.name}"
                shutil.move(str(wav), str(CONFUSABLE_DIR / new_name))
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"    ✗ Error: {e}")
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)
    
    gc.collect()

confusable_count = len(list(CONFUSABLE_DIR.glob('*.wav')))
print(f"\n✓ Confusable negatives: {confusable_count} samples")</cell id="cell-16">

from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips
from microwakeword.audio.spectrograms import SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja.ragged import RaggedMmap

CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'confusable_negatives'

# Check if features already exist
confusable_mmap = CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR / 'training' / 'wakeword_mmap'
if confusable_mmap.exists():
    print("✓ Confusable features already exist, skipping generation")
else:
    print("Generating spectrogram features from confusable negatives...")
    print(f"  Source: {CONFUSABLE_DIR} ({confusable_count} wav files)")
    print(f"  Output: {CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR}")
    print()
    
    # Create Clips object
    confusable_clips = Clips(
        input_directory=str(CONFUSABLE_DIR),
        file_pattern='*.wav',
        max_clip_duration_s=None,
        remove_silence=False,
        random_split_seed=42,
        split_count=0.1,  # 10% for validation
    )
    
    CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    for split in ["training", "validation"]:
        out_dir = CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR / split
        out_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        
        split_name = "train" if split == "training" else "validation"
        repetition = 5 if split == "training" else 1  # Fewer repeats than positives
        
        spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(
            clips=confusable_clips,
            augmenter=augmentation,
            slide_frames=10,
            step_ms=10,
        )
        
        print(f"  Generating {split} features (repeat={repetition})...")
        RaggedMmap.from_generator(
            out_dir=str(out_dir / 'wakeword_mmap'),
            sample_generator=spectrograms.spectrogram_generator(
                split=split_name, 
                repeat=repetition
            ),
            batch_size=100,
            verbose=True,
        )
    
    print("\n✓ Confusable feature generation complete")

# Verify
confusable_train = RaggedMmap(str(CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR / 'training' / 'wakeword_mmap'), mode='r')
confusable_val = RaggedMmap(str(CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR / 'validation' / 'wakeword_mmap'), mode='r')
print(f"  Confusable training features: {len(confusable_train)} spectrograms")
print(f"  Confusable validation features: {len(confusable_val)} spectrograms")</cell id="cell-17">

# Install torchcodec FIRST (required for datasets audio decoding)

import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

AUDIOSET_DIR = AUGMENTATION_DIR / 'audioset'

else:
    try:
        from datasets import load_dataset
        import soundfile as sf
        print("Loading AudioSet subset via datasets library...")
        
        # Load balanced subset with streaming
        ds = load_dataset(
            "agkphysics/AudioSet", 
            split="train",
            streaming=True,
        )
        
        # Save first 500 audio samples as wav files
        count = 0
        max_samples = 500
        
        for sample in ds:
            if count >= max_samples:
                break
            try:
                audio = sample['audio']
                wav_path = AUDIOSET_DIR / f"audioset_{count:04d}.wav"
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio['array'], audio['sampling_rate'])
                count += 1
                if count % 100 == 0:
                    print(f"  Saved {count}/{max_samples} samples")
            except Exception:
                continue  # Skip problematic samples
        
        print(f"Done! Saved {count} background audio samples")

    except Exception as e:
        print(f"AudioSet loading failed: {e}")
        print("Background augmentation will use MIT impulse responses only.")</cell id="cell-20">

from microwakeword.audio.augmentation import Augmentation

# Verify we have background noise files

    raise RuntimeError(f"No AudioSet files found in {AUDIOSET_DIR}! Re-run AudioSet download cell.")

augmentation = Augmentation(
    augmentation_duration_s=3.2,

        "SevenBandParametricEQ": 0.1,
        "TanhDistortion": 0.1,
        "PitchShift": 0.1,
        "BandStopFilter": 0.1,
        "AddColorNoise": 0.1,
        "AddBackgroundNoise": 0.75,
        "Gain": 1.0,
        "RIR": 0.5,
    },
    impulse_paths=[str(MIT_IR_DIR / 'Audio')],
    background_paths=[str(AUDIOSET_DIR)],
)
print(f"Augmentation configured with {len(audioset_files)} background noise files")</cell id="cell-23">

#=============================================================================
# This cell must run AFTER augmentation is configured (cell above)

CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'confusable_negatives'

# Check if features already exist
confusable_mmap = CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR / 'training' / 'wakeword_mmap'
if confusable_mmap.exists():
    print("✓ Confusable features already exist, skipping generation")
else:
    print("Generating spectrogram features from confusable negatives...")
    print(f"  Source: {CONFUSABLE_DIR} ({confusable_count} wav files)")
    print(f"  Output: {CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR}")
    print()
    
    # Create Clips object
    confusable_clips = Clips(
        input_directory=str(CONFUSABLE_DIR),
        file_pattern='*.wav',
        max_clip_duration_s=None,
        remove_silence=False,
        random_split_seed=42,
        split_count=0.1,  # 10% for validation
    )
    
    CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    for split in ["training", "validation"]:
        out_dir = CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR / split
        out_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        
        split_name = "train" if split == "training" else "validation"
        repetition = 5 if split == "training" else 1  # Fewer repeats than positives
        
        spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(
            clips=confusable_clips,
            augmenter=augmentation,
            slide_frames=10,
            step_ms=10,
        )
        
        print(f"  Generating {split} features (repeat={repetition})...")
        RaggedMmap.from_generator(
            out_dir=str(out_dir / 'wakeword_mmap'),
            sample_generator=spectrograms.spectrogram_generator(
                split=split_name, 
                repeat=repetition
            ),
            batch_size=100,
            verbose=True,
        )
    
    print("\n✓ Confusable feature generation complete")

# Verify
confusable_train = RaggedMmap(str(CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR / 'training' / 'wakeword_mmap'), mode='r')
confusable_val = RaggedMmap(str(CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR / 'validation' / 'wakeword_mmap'), mode='r')
print(f"  Confusable training features: {len(confusable_train)} spectrograms")
print(f"  Confusable validation features: {len(confusable_val)} spectrograms")

Good questions! Let me clarify:

### 1. step_ms (10ms stride)

**Don't change this.** Here's why:

- `step_ms=10` is the **spectrogram stride** - how often features are computed
- This is baked into the microWakeWord architecture and must match inference
- Your ESP32 code runs inference every 10ms to match this
- Changing it would require updating both training AND inference code

The 10ms stride isn't about "detection speed" - it's about **temporal resolution**. Coarser strides (30ms) would actually make it harder to distinguish "Hey" from "Hey Daisy" because you'd have fewer frames to analyze the phrase timing.

**The partial detection issue is a training data problem, not a temporal resolution problem.** The confusable negatives should fix it.

### 2. Training steps (20K)

**20K is reasonable**, here's the math:

- Batch size: 1024
- Steps: 20,000  
- Samples seen: ~20 million
- Your dataset: ~300-500K spectrograms
- Each sample seen: ~40-60 times (with augmentation variation)

For wake word models, you need many passes because:
- Small models have limited capacity → must generalize well
- Augmentation creates different versions each epoch
- You're now adding confusable negatives which adds complexity

**Options:**
- **Keep 20K** - safe choice, might plateau early but won't underfit
- **Reduce to 15K** - if you want faster training, likely still sufficient
- **Watch the logs** - if accuracy plateaus around step 10K, you can stop early next time

I'd suggest keeping 20K for this retrain since you're adding significant new negative data. You can reduce it next time if validation accuracy plateaus early.

<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-4"># Patch microWakeWord for TensorFlow 2.17 compatibility
# TF 2.17 returns numpy arrays directly instead of tensors, so .numpy() calls fail

import re

train_py = '/workspace/microWakeWord/microwakeword/train.py'

with open(train_py, 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Check if already patched
if 'np.asarray' not in content:
    # Replace patterns like: result["fp"].numpy() -> np.asarray(result["fp"])
    # This handles both tensor (needs .numpy()) and numpy array (already is) cases
    patched = re.sub(
        r'(\w+)\[(["\'])(\w+)\2\]\.numpy\(\)',
        r'np.asarray(\1["\3"])',
        content
    )
    
    with open(train_py, 'w') as f:
        f.write(patched)
    
    print("✓ Patched train.py for TensorFlow 2.17 compatibility")
else:
    print("✓ train.py already patched")</cell id="cell-4">

✓ Patched train.py for TensorFlow 2.17 compatibility

# PHASE 3: XTTS GENERATION (SKIP IF DATA EXISTS)
#=============================================================================
if SKIP_GENERATION:
    print("✓ Skipping XTTS generation - using existing data")
else:
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("PHASE 3: XTTS-v2 GENERATION")
    print("="*60)

    import torch
    from TTS.api import TTS

    # Build task list: (variation_text, speaker_wav, output_path)
    xtts_tasks = []
    for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
        for speaker_wav in speaker_files:
            speaker_name = Path(speaker_wav).stem
            output_path = str(training_dir / f"xtts_var{i}_{speaker_name}.wav")
            # Skip if already generated (resume support)
            if not Path(output_path).exists():
                xtts_tasks.append((variation, speaker_wav, output_path))

    total_tasks = len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * len(speaker_files)
    already_done = total_tasks - len(xtts_tasks)

    print(f"  Total XTTS tasks: {total_tasks}")
    if already_done > 0:
        print(f"  Already completed: {already_done} (resuming...)")
    print(f"  Remaining: {len(xtts_tasks)}")

    if len(xtts_tasks) > 0:
        # Load XTTS model
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
        print(f"\n  Loading XTTS-v2 on {device}...")
        xtts = TTS("tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2").to(device)
        print("  Model loaded!")
        
        # Sequential generation with progress
        failed = 0
        for idx, (variation, speaker_wav, output_path) in enumerate(xtts_tasks):
            # Progress every 80 samples (1 variation * 80 voices)
            if idx % 80 == 0:
                pct = 100 * (idx + already_done) // total_tasks
                print(f"  Progress: {idx + already_done}/{total_tasks} ({pct}%)")
            
            try:
                xtts.tts_to_file(
                    text=variation,
                    file_path=output_path,
                    speaker_wav=speaker_wav,
                    language="en"
                )
            except Exception as e:
                failed += 1
                if failed <= 5:  # Only show first 5 errors
                    print(f"    ✗ {Path(output_path).stem}: {e}")
        
        # Cleanup
        del xtts
        gc.collect()
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        
        if failed > 0:
            print(f"\n  ⚠ {failed} samples failed")

    xtts_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('xtts_*.wav')))
    print(f"\n✓ XTTS complete: {xtts_count} samples")
    gc.collect()</cell id="cell-12">

    raise RuntimeError(f"No AudioSet files found in {AUDIOSET_DIR}! Re-run AudioSet download cell.")

    augmentation_duration_s=3.2,
    augmentation_probabilities={
        "SevenBandParametricEQ": 0.1,
        "TanhDistortion": 0.1,
        "PitchShift": 0.1,
        "BandStopFilter": 0.1,
        "AddColorNoise": 0.1,
        "AddBackgroundNoise": 0.75,
        "Gain": 1.0,
        "RIR": 0.5,
    },
    impulse_paths=[str(MIT_IR_DIR / 'Audio')],

)

<cell id="cell-23"># Cell 11: Generate spectrogram features from audio samples
from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips
from microwakeword.audio.spectrograms import SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja.ragged import RaggedMmap
import os

POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'

# Check if features already exist
train_mmap = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'training' / 'wakeword_mmap'
if train_mmap.exists():
    print("✓ Features already exist, skipping generation")
else:
    print("Generating spectrogram features from audio samples...")
    print(f"  Source: {training_dir} ({len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))} wav files)")
    print(f"  Output: {POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR}")
    print()
    
    # Create Clips object pointing to audio files
    clips = Clips(
        input_directory=str(training_dir),
        file_pattern='*.wav',
        max_clip_duration_s=None,
        remove_silence=False,
        random_split_seed=10,
        split_count=0.1,  # 10% for validation
    )
    
    # Create output directories
    POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    splits = ["training", "validation"]
    for split in splits:
        out_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / split
        out_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        
        split_name = "train" if split == "training" else "validation"
        repetition = 10 if split == "training" else 1  # More augmented copies for training
        
        spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(
            clips=clips,
            augmenter=augmentation,
            slide_frames=10,
            step_ms=10,
        )
        
        print(f"  Generating {split} features (repeat={repetition})...")
        RaggedMmap.from_generator(
            out_dir=str(out_dir / 'wakeword_mmap'),
            sample_generator=spectrograms.spectrogram_generator(
                split=split_name, 
                repeat=repetition
            ),
            batch_size=100,
            verbose=True,
        )
    
    print("\n✓ Feature generation complete")

# Verify
train_features = RaggedMmap(str(POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'training' / 'wakeword_mmap'), mode='r')
val_features = RaggedMmap(str(POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'validation' / 'wakeword_mmap'), mode='r')

    # Create Clips object
    confusable_clips = Clips(
        input_directory=str(CONFUSABLE_DIR),
        file_pattern='*.wav',
        max_clip_duration_s=None,
        remove_silence=False,
        random_split_seed=42,
        split_count=0.1,  # 10% for validation
    )
    
    CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    for split in ["training", "validation"]:
        out_dir = CONFUSABLE_FEATURES_DIR / split
        out_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        
        split_name = "train" if split == "training" else "validation"
        repetition = 5 if split == "training" else 1  # Fewer repeats than positives
        
        spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(
            clips=confusable_clips,
            augmenter=augmentation,
            slide_frames=10,
            step_ms=10,
        )
        
        print(f"  Generating {split} features (repeat={repetition})...")
        RaggedMmap.from_generator(
            out_dir=str(out_dir / 'wakeword_mmap'),
            sample_generator=spectrograms.spectrogram_generator(
                split=split_name, 
                repeat=repetition
            ),
            batch_size=100,
            verbose=True,
        )
    
    print("\n✓ Confusable feature generation complete")

    45→def load_config(flags, model_module):
    46→    """Loads the training configuration from the specified yaml file.
    47→
    48→    Args:
    49→        flags (argparse.Namespace): command line flags
    50→        model_module (module): python module for loading the model
    51→
    52→    Returns:
    53→        dict: dictionary containing training configuration
    54→    """
    55→    config_filename = flags.training_config
    56→    config = yaml.load(open(config_filename, "r").read(), yaml.Loader)
    57→
    58→    config["summaries_dir"] = os.path.join(config["train_dir"], "logs/")
    59→
    60→    config["stride"] = flags.__dict__.get("stride", 1)
    61→    config["window_step_ms"] = config.get("window_step_ms", 20)
    62→
    63→    # Default preprocessor settings
    64→    preprocessor_sample_rate = 16000  # Hz
    65→    preprocessor_window_size = 30  # ms
    66→    preprocessor_window_step = config["window_step_ms"]  # ms
    67→
    68→    desired_samples = int(preprocessor_sample_rate * config["clip_duration_ms"] / 1000)
    69→
    70→    window_size_samples = int(
    71→        preprocessor_sample_rate * preprocessor_window_size / 1000
    72→    )
    73→    window_step_samples = int(
    74→        config["stride"] * preprocessor_sample_rate * preprocessor_window_step / 1000
    75→    )
    76→
    77→    length_minus_window = desired_samples - window_size_samples
    78→
    79→    if length_minus_window < 0:
    80→        config["spectrogram_length_final_layer"] = 0
    81→    else:
    82→        config["spectrogram_length_final_layer"] = 1 + int(
    83→            length_minus_window / window_step_samples
    84→        )
    85→
    86→    config["spectrogram_length"] = config[
    87→        "spectrogram_length_final_layer"
    88→    ] + model_module.spectrogram_slices_dropped(flags)
    89→
    90→    config["flags"] = flags.__dict__
    91→
    92→    config["training_input_shape"] = modes.get_input_data_shape(
    93→        config, modes.Modes.TRAINING
    94→    )
    95→
    96→    return config
    97→

    99→def train_model(config, model, data_processor, restore_checkpoint):
   100→    """Trains a model.
   101→
   102→    Args:
   103→        config (dict): dictionary containing training configuration
   104→        model (Keras model): model architecture to train
   105→        data_processor (FeatureHandler): feature handler that loads spectrogram data
   106→        restore_checkpoint (bool): Whether to restore from checkpoint if model exists
   107→
   108→    Raises:
   109→        ValueError: If the model exists but the training flag isn't set
   110→    """
   111→    try:
   112→        os.makedirs(config["train_dir"])
   113→        os.mkdir(config["summaries_dir"])
   114→    except OSError:
   115→        if restore_checkpoint:
   116→            pass
   117→        else:
   118→            raise ValueError(
   119→                "model already exists in folder %s" % config["train_dir"]
   120→            ) from None
   121→    config_fname = os.path.join(config["train_dir"], "training_config.yaml")
   122→
   123→    with open(config_fname, "w") as outfile:
   124→        yaml.dump(config, outfile, default_flow_style=False)
   125→
   126→    utils.save_model_summary(model, config["train_dir"])
   127→
   128→    train.train(model, config, data_processor)

```
## Key Resources for Compatibility

## Where to Find the Official Matrix

To determine which version of CUDA and cuDNN you need, refer to the TensorFlow installation documentation. They provide a compatibility matrix listing supported versions.      ```cpp
```
     ```cpp
     #define PROBABILITY_CUTOFF  0.99f
     #define SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE 10
     #define MIN_HIGH_FRAMES     10      // Require 10/10 frames above MIN_FRAME_PROB
     #define MIN_FRAME_PROB      0.5f   // Individual frame threshold
     #define COOLDOWN_MS         1500   // Ignore detections for 1.5s after trigger
     ```
     - Detection function with cooldown:
     ```cpp
     bool detectWakeword(float probability) {
       // Add to sliding window
       probability_window[window_pos] = probability;
       window_pos = (window_pos + 1) % SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;
       if (window_pos == 0) { window_filled = true; }
       if (!window_filled) { return false; }
       
       // Cooldown check
       if (millis() - last_detection_ms < COOLDOWN_MS) { return false; }
       
       // Calculate average probability AND count high frames
       float avg = 0.0f;
       int high_frames = 0;
       for (int i = 0; i < SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
         avg += probability_window[i];
         if (probability_window[i] >= MIN_FRAME_PROB) { high_frames++; }
       }
       avg /= SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;
       
       if (avg >= PROBABILITY_CUTOFF && high_frames >= MIN_HIGH_FRAMES) {
         last_detection_ms = millis();
         return true;
       }
       return false;
     }
     ```

```
<cell id="cell-0"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type># microWakeWord Training Notebook

Train a custom wake word detection model compatible with ESP32-S3.

## Overview

This notebook trains models compatible with `wakeword_pretrained_test.ino`:
- **Input**: 40-bin log-mel spectrogram features (30ms window, 10ms stride)
- **Architecture**: MixNet-based streaming model
- **Output**: Quantized TFLite model for ESP32

Based on: https://github.com/kahrendt/microWakeWord</cell id="cell-0">

<cell id="cell-4"># Patch microWakeWord for TensorFlow 2.17 compatibility
# TF 2.17 returns numpy arrays directly instead of tensors, so .numpy() calls fail

import re

train_py = '/workspace/microWakeWord/microwakeword/train.py'

with open(train_py, 'r') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Check if already patched
if 'np.asarray' not in content:
    # Replace patterns like: result["fp"].numpy() -> np.asarray(result["fp"])
    # This handles both tensor (needs .numpy()) and numpy array (already is) cases
    patched = re.sub(
        r'(\w+)\[(["\'])(\w+)\2\]\.numpy\(\)',
        r'np.asarray(\1["\3"])',
        content
    )
    
    with open(train_py, 'w') as f:
        f.write(patched)
    
    print("✓ Patched train.py for TensorFlow 2.17 compatibility")
else:
    print("✓ train.py already patched")</cell id="cell-4">

✓ Patched train.py for TensorFlow 2.17 compatibility

import urllib.request
import librosa
import soundfile as sf

speaker_voices_dir = WORK_DIR / 'speaker_voices'
speaker_voices_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

speaker_files = []
for speaker in TED_SPEAKERS:
    for sample_idx in range(SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER):
        wav_path = speaker_voices_dir / f'ted_{speaker}_{sample_idx}.wav'
        mp3_path = speaker_voices_dir / f'ted_{speaker}_{sample_idx}.mp3'
        
        if not wav_path.exists():
            try:
                url = f'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/audio-samples/audio-samples.github.io/master/samples/mp3/ted_speakers/{speaker}/sample-{sample_idx}.mp3'
                urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, mp3_path)
                audio, sr = librosa.load(mp3_path, sr=16000, mono=True)
                if len(audio) > 6 * 16000:
                    audio = audio[:6 * 16000]
                sf.write(str(wav_path), audio, 16000)
                mp3_path.unlink()
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  ✗ {speaker}/sample-{sample_idx}: {e}")
                continue
        speaker_files.append(str(wav_path))
    print(f"  ✓ {speaker} ({SAMPLES_PER_SPEAKER} samples)")

# PHASE 3: XTTS GENERATION (SKIP IF DATA EXISTS)
#=============================================================================
if SKIP_GENERATION:
    print("✓ Skipping XTTS generation - using existing data")
else:
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("PHASE 3: XTTS-v2 GENERATION")
    print("="*60)

    import torch
    from TTS.api import TTS

    # Build task list: (variation_text, speaker_wav, output_path)
    xtts_tasks = []
    for i, variation in enumerate(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS):
        for speaker_wav in speaker_files:
            speaker_name = Path(speaker_wav).stem
            output_path = str(training_dir / f"xtts_var{i}_{speaker_name}.wav")
            # Skip if already generated (resume support)
            if not Path(output_path).exists():
                xtts_tasks.append((variation, speaker_wav, output_path))

    total_tasks = len(PHONETIC_VARIATIONS) * len(speaker_files)
    already_done = total_tasks - len(xtts_tasks)

    print(f"  Total XTTS tasks: {total_tasks}")
    if already_done > 0:
        print(f"  Already completed: {already_done} (resuming...)")
    print(f"  Remaining: {len(xtts_tasks)}")

    if len(xtts_tasks) > 0:
        # Load XTTS model
        device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
        print(f"\n  Loading XTTS-v2 on {device}...")
        xtts = TTS("tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2").to(device)
        print("  Model loaded!")
        
        # Sequential generation with progress
        failed = 0
        for idx, (variation, speaker_wav, output_path) in enumerate(xtts_tasks):
            # Progress every 80 samples (1 variation * 80 voices)
            if idx % 80 == 0:
                pct = 100 * (idx + already_done) // total_tasks
                print(f"  Progress: {idx + already_done}/{total_tasks} ({pct}%)")
            
            try:
                xtts.tts_to_file(
                    text=variation,
                    file_path=output_path,
                    speaker_wav=speaker_wav,
                    language="en"
                )
            except Exception as e:
                failed += 1
                if failed <= 5:  # Only show first 5 errors
                    print(f"    ✗ {Path(output_path).stem}: {e}")
        
        # Cleanup
        del xtts
        gc.collect()
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        
        if failed > 0:
            print(f"\n  ⚠ {failed} samples failed")

    xtts_count = len(list(training_dir.glob('xtts_*.wav')))
    print(f"\n✓ XTTS complete: {xtts_count} samples")
    gc.collect()</cell id="cell-12">

    'dinner_party_eval.zip': 'dinner_party_eval',
}

BASE_URL = 'https://huggingface.co/datasets/kahrendt/microwakeword/resolve/main'

print("Downloading negative features (this may take several minutes)...")
for zip_name, folder_name in NEGATIVE_FILES.items():
    zip_path = NEGATIVE_DIR / zip_name
    extract_dir = NEGATIVE_DIR / folder_name
    
    if not extract_dir.exists():
        print(f"  Downloading {zip_name}...")
        !wget -q --show-progress -O {zip_path} '{BASE_URL}/{zip_name}'
        
        if zip_path.exists() and zip_path.stat().st_size > 1000:
            print(f"  Extracting {zip_name}...")
            with zipfile.ZipFile(zip_path, 'r') as z:
                z.extractall(NEGATIVE_DIR)
            zip_path.unlink()  # Remove zip to save space
        else:
            print(f"  WARNING: {zip_name} download failed")
    else:
        print(f"  {folder_name} already exists")

from microwakeword.audio.clips import Clips
from microwakeword.audio.spectrograms import SpectrogramGeneration
from mmap_ninja.ragged import RaggedMmap
import os

POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR = FEATURES_DIR / 'positive'

# Check if features already exist
train_mmap = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'training' / 'wakeword_mmap'
if train_mmap.exists():
    print("✓ Features already exist, skipping generation")
else:
    print("Generating spectrogram features from audio samples...")
    print(f"  Source: {training_dir} ({len(list(training_dir.glob('*.wav')))} wav files)")
    print(f"  Output: {POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR}")
    print()
    
    # Create Clips object pointing to audio files
    clips = Clips(
        input_directory=str(training_dir),
        file_pattern='*.wav',
        max_clip_duration_s=None,
        remove_silence=False,
        random_split_seed=10,
        split_count=0.1,  # 10% for validation
    )
    
    # Create output directories
    POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    splits = ["training", "validation"]
    for split in splits:
        out_dir = POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / split
        out_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        
        split_name = "train" if split == "training" else "validation"

        spectrograms = SpectrogramGeneration(

            slide_frames=10,
            step_ms=10,

        print(f"  Generating {split} features (repeat={repetition})...")
        RaggedMmap.from_generator(
            out_dir=str(out_dir / 'wakeword_mmap'),
            sample_generator=spectrograms.spectrogram_generator(
                split=split_name, 
                repeat=repetition
            ),
            batch_size=100,
            verbose=True,
        )
    
    print("\n✓ Feature generation complete")

# Verify

val_features = RaggedMmap(str(POSITIVE_FEATURES_DIR / 'validation' / 'wakeword_mmap'), mode='r')
print(f"  Training features: {len(train_features)} spectrograms")
print(f"  Validation features: {len(val_features)} spectrograms")</cell id="cell-23">

import shutil
import os
import sys
import site

print("="*60)
print("GPU SETUP & VERIFICATION")
print("="*60)

#=============================================================================
# STEP 1: Find CUDA/cuDNN libraries (including pip-installed ones)
#=============================================================================
print("\n1. Searching for CUDA/cuDNN libraries...")

cuda_lib_paths = []

# First, check pip-installed nvidia packages (these take priority!)
# They're typically in site-packages/nvidia/*/lib/
for site_path in site.getsitepackages() + [site.getusersitepackages()]:
    nvidia_path = os.path.join(site_path, 'nvidia')
    if os.path.exists(nvidia_path):
        for pkg in os.listdir(nvidia_path):
            lib_path = os.path.join(nvidia_path, pkg, 'lib')
            if os.path.exists(lib_path):
                cuda_lib_paths.append(lib_path)
                cudnn_files = [f for f in os.listdir(lib_path) if 'cudnn' in f.lower()]
                if cudnn_files:
                    print(f"   ✓ {lib_path}")
                    print(f"      cuDNN: {cudnn_files[:3]}")

# Also check uv venv's site-packages
venv_nvidia = '/workspace/.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/nvidia'
if os.path.exists(venv_nvidia):
    for pkg in os.listdir(venv_nvidia):
        lib_path = os.path.join(venv_nvidia, pkg, 'lib')
        if os.path.exists(lib_path) and lib_path not in cuda_lib_paths:
            cuda_lib_paths.append(lib_path)
            cudnn_files = [f for f in os.listdir(lib_path) if 'cudnn' in f.lower()]
            if cudnn_files:
                print(f"   ✓ {lib_path} (venv)")
                print(f"      cuDNN: {cudnn_files[:3]}")

# Then check system paths
system_paths = [
    '/usr/local/cuda/lib64',
    '/usr/local/cuda-12/lib64',
    '/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu',
]

for path in system_paths:
    if os.path.exists(path) and path not in cuda_lib_paths:
        cuda_lib_paths.append(path)
        cudnn_files = [f for f in os.listdir(path) if 'cudnn' in f.lower()]
        status = "✓" if cudnn_files else "·"
        print(f"   {status} {path} (system)")
        if cudnn_files:
            print(f"      cuDNN: {cudnn_files[:3]}")

if not cuda_lib_paths:
    raise RuntimeError("No CUDA library paths found!")

#=============================================================================
# STEP 2: Set environment variables (pip-installed first!)
#=============================================================================
print("\n2. Setting environment variables...")

ld_library_path = ':'.join(cuda_lib_paths) + ':' + os.environ.get('LD_LIBRARY_PATH', '')
os.environ['LD_LIBRARY_PATH'] = ld_library_path
os.environ['CUDA_HOME'] = '/usr/local/cuda'
os.environ['TF_FORCE_GPU_ALLOW_GROWTH'] = 'true'
os.environ['TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL'] = '2'

print(f"   LD_LIBRARY_PATH (first 3 paths):")
for p in cuda_lib_paths[:3]:
    print(f"      {p}")

#=============================================================================
# STEP 3: Verify GPU with nvidia-smi
#=============================================================================
print("\n3. nvidia-smi check:")
!nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total --format=csv,noheader 2>/dev/null || echo "   ERROR: nvidia-smi not found!"

#=============================================================================
# STEP 4: Test TensorFlow GPU detection in subprocess
#=============================================================================
print("\n4. Testing TensorFlow GPU in subprocess...")

test_script = '''
import os
os.environ["TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL"] = "3"
import tensorflow as tf
gpus = tf.config.list_physical_devices("GPU")
print(f"TF_VERSION: {tf.__version__}")
print(f"GPU_COUNT: {len(gpus)}")
for gpu in gpus:
    print(f"GPU_FOUND: {gpu.name}")
if len(gpus) == 0:
    print("ERROR: No GPU found by TensorFlow!")
    # Show what cuDNN TF found
    print("Checking cuDNN...")
    try:
        from tensorflow.python.platform import build_info
        print(f"TF build info: {build_info.build_info}")
    except:
        pass
    import sys
    sys.exit(1)
'''

with open('/tmp/tf_gpu_test.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(test_script)

result = !LD_LIBRARY_PATH="{ld_library_path}" uv run python /tmp/tf_gpu_test.py 2>&1 | grep -v "Unable to register"
for line in result:
    print(f"   {line}")

if any("ERROR: No GPU" in line for line in result) or not any("GPU_FOUND" in line for line in result):
    print("\n" + "!"*60)
    print("FATAL: TensorFlow cannot find GPU!")
    print("!"*60)
    print("\nTry: Restart kernel and re-run cell-3 to reinstall cuDNN 9.1")
    raise RuntimeError("GPU not available - stopping to prevent slow CPU training")

print("\n" + "="*60)
print("✓ GPU VERIFIED - Proceeding with training")
print("="*60)

#=============================================================================
# TRAINING
#=============================================================================
if MODEL_DIR.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(MODEL_DIR)
    print(f"\nCleaned up: {MODEL_DIR}")

print()
print("Starting training...")
print(f"  Batch size: {BATCH_SIZE}")
print(f"  Training steps: 20,000")
print(f"  Model: 128 filters (larger)")
print()

# Run training with explicit LD_LIBRARY_PATH
!LD_LIBRARY_PATH="{ld_library_path}" \
 CUDA_HOME="/usr/local/cuda" \
 TF_FORCE_GPU_ALLOW_GROWTH="true" \
 uv run python -m microwakeword.model_train_eval \
    --training_config='{config_path}' \
    --train 1 \
    --test_tflite_streaming_quantized 1 \
    --use_weights 'best_weights' \
    mixednet \
    --pointwise_filters '128,128,128,128' \
    --repeat_in_block '1,1,1,1' \
    --mixconv_kernel_sizes '[5], [7,11], [9,15], [23]' \
    --residual_connection '0,0,0,0' \
    --first_conv_filters 64 \
    --first_conv_kernel_size 5 \
```

```
cuda_lib_paths = system_cuda_paths + venv_cuda_paths

if not system_cuda_paths:
    print("\n⚠️  WARNING: No system cuDNN found!")
    print("   TF 2.18 may fail - it needs cuDNN 9.3+, PyTorch bundles 9.1")

#=============================================================================
# STEP 2: Set environment variables (SYSTEM cuDNN first!)
#=============================================================================
print("\n2. Setting environment variables...")

# System paths FIRST, then venv paths
ld_library_path = ':'.join(cuda_lib_paths) + ':' + os.environ.get('LD_LIBRARY_PATH', '')
os.environ['LD_LIBRARY_PATH'] = ld_library_path
os.environ['CUDA_HOME'] = '/usr/local/cuda'
os.environ['TF_FORCE_GPU_ALLOW_GROWTH'] = 'true'
os.environ['TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL'] = '2'

print(f"   LD_LIBRARY_PATH order (for TF 2.18 + cuDNN 9.3+):")
for i, p in enumerate(cuda_lib_paths[:4]):
    priority = "HIGH" if p in system_cuda_paths else "low"
    print(f"      [{priority}] {p}")

#=============================================================================
# STEP 3: Verify GPU with nvidia-smi
#=============================================================================
print("\n3. nvidia-smi check:")
!nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total --format=csv,noheader 2>/dev/null || echo "   ERROR: nvidia-smi not found!"

#=============================================================================
# STEP 4: Test TensorFlow GPU detection in subprocess
#=============================================================================
print("\n4. Testing TensorFlow GPU in subprocess...")

test_script = '''
import os
os.environ["TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL"] = "3"
import tensorflow as tf
gpus = tf.config.list_physical_devices("GPU")
print(f"TF_VERSION: {tf.__version__}")
print(f"GPU_COUNT: {len(gpus)}")
for gpu in gpus:
    print(f"GPU_FOUND: {gpu.name}")
if len(gpus) == 0:
    print("ERROR: No GPU found by TensorFlow!")
    # Check cuDNN version TF is using
    try:
        from tensorflow.python.platform import build_info
        print(f"TF build cudnn_version: {build_info.build_info.get('cudnn_version', 'unknown')}")
    except:
        pass
    import sys
    sys.exit(1)
else:
    print("SUCCESS: GPU detected!")
'''

with open('/tmp/tf_gpu_test.py', 'w') as f:
    f.write(test_script)

result = !LD_LIBRARY_PATH="{ld_library_path}" uv run python /tmp/tf_gpu_test.py 2>&1 | grep -v "Unable to register"
for line in result:
    print(f"   {line}")

if any("ERROR: No GPU" in line for line in result) or not any("GPU_FOUND" in line for line in result):
    print("\n" + "!"*60)
    print("FATAL: TensorFlow cannot find GPU!")
    print("!"*60)
    print("\nDebugging info:")
    print("  - TF 2.18 requires cuDNN 9.3+")
    print("  - System should have cuDNN 9.10.2 in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu")
    print("  - Check that system path is FIRST in LD_LIBRARY_PATH above")
    raise RuntimeError("GPU not available - stopping to prevent slow CPU training")

print("\n" + "="*60)
print("✓ GPU VERIFIED - Proceeding with training")
print("="*60)

#=============================================================================
# TRAINING
#=============================================================================
if MODEL_DIR.exists():
    shutil.rmtree(MODEL_DIR)
    print(f"\nCleaned up: {MODEL_DIR}")

print()
print("Starting training...")
print(f"  Batch size: {BATCH_SIZE}")
print(f"  Training steps: 20,000")
print(f"  Model: 128 filters (larger)")
print()

# Run training with explicit LD_LIBRARY_PATH (system cuDNN first!)
!LD_LIBRARY_PATH="{ld_library_path}" \
 CUDA_HOME="/usr/local/cuda" \
 TF_FORCE_GPU_ALLOW_GROWTH="true" \
 uv run python -m microwakeword.model_train_eval \
    --training_config='{config_path}' \
    --train 1 \

    --use_weights 'best_weights' \

    --stride 3
```

   403→bool captureAudio() {
   404→  // Only read if we have space in buffer
   405→  int space_available = AUDIO_BUFFER_SIZE - audio_buffer_pos;
   406→  if (space_available < 256) {
   407→    return true;  // Buffer has data, let it be processed first
   408→  }
   409→
   410→  // Read smaller chunks more frequently for smoother audio
   411→  int samples_to_read = min(256, space_available);
   412→  size_t bytes_read;
   413→  if (i2s_read(I2S_NUM_0, i2s_buffer, samples_to_read * 4, &bytes_read, 10) != ESP_OK) {
   414→    return false;
   415→  }
   416→
   417→  int samples = bytes_read / 4;
   418→
   419→  // Track audio levels for debug
   420→  static int audio_debug = 0;
   421→  int32_t max_sample = 0;
   422→
   423→  for (int i = 0; i < samples; i++) {
   424→    // Convert 32-bit I2S to 16-bit
   425→    // INMP441 outputs 24-bit in MSB of 32-bit word, shift right to get 16-bit
   426→    int32_t sample = i2s_buffer[i] >> 14;  // >>14 for moderate gain
   427→    audio_buffer[audio_buffer_pos++] = constrain(sample, -32768, 32767);
   428→
   429→    if (abs(sample) > max_sample) max_sample = abs(sample);
   430→  }
   431→
   432→#if DEBUG_FEATURES
   433→  if (++audio_debug >= 300) {
   434→    audio_debug = 0;
   435→    Serial.printf("Audio: amp=%ld, buf=%d\n", max_sample, audio_buffer_pos);
   436→  }
   437→#endif
   438→
   439→  return true;
   440→}

   442→float runInference() {
   443→  // Copy 3 frames of features to input tensor
   444→  int total_features = FEATURE_FRAMES * FEATURE_BINS;  // 3 * 40 = 120
   445→
   446→  // Debug: print quant params once
   447→  static bool printed_params = false;
   448→  if (!printed_params) {
   449→    printed_params = true;
   450→    Serial.printf("\n=== INFERENCE DEBUG ===\n");
   451→    Serial.printf("Input type=%d, scale=%.6f, zp=%d\n",
   452→      input_tensor->type, input_tensor->params.scale, input_tensor->params.zero_point);
   453→    Serial.printf("Output type=%d, scale=%.6f, zp=%d\n",
   454→      output_tensor->type, output_tensor->params.scale, output_tensor->params.zero_point);
   455→    Serial.printf("Input bytes=%d, Output bytes=%d\n",
   456→      input_tensor->bytes, output_tensor->bytes);
   457→  }
   458→
   459→  if (input_tensor->type == kTfLiteInt8) {
   460→    int8_t* input_data = input_tensor->data.int8;
   461→
   462→    // Use ESPHome's proven formula directly
   463→    for (int i = 0; i < total_features; i++) {
   464→      int32_t scaled = ((int32_t)feature_buffer[i] * 256 + 333) / 666 - 128;
   465→      input_data[i] = constrain(scaled, -128, 127);
   466→    }
   467→
   468→    // Debug: show first few input values once
   469→    static int input_debug = 0;
   470→    if (++input_debug == 50) {
   471→      Serial.printf("Input[0-5]: %d,%d,%d,%d,%d,%d\n",
   472→        input_data[0], input_data[1], input_data[2],
   473→        input_data[3], input_data[4], input_data[5]);
   474→    }
   475→  } else {
   476→    // Float model
   477→    float* input_data = input_tensor->data.f;
   478→    for (int i = 0; i < total_features; i++) {
   479→      input_data[i] = feature_buffer[i] / 25.6f;
   480→    }
   481→  }
   482→
   483→  // Run inference
   484→  if (interpreter->Invoke() != kTfLiteOk) {
   485→    Serial.println("Invoke failed");
   486→    return 0.0f;
   487→  }
   488→
   489→  // Get output probability
   490→  float probability;
   491→
   492→  // Debug: show raw output once
   493→  static int out_debug = 0;
   494→
   495→  if (output_tensor->type == kTfLiteUInt8) {
   496→    uint8_t output_value = output_tensor->data.uint8[0];
   497→    probability = (output_value - output_tensor->params.zero_point) *
   498→                  output_tensor->params.scale;
   499→    if (++out_debug == 50) {
   500→      Serial.printf("Raw output uint8=%u, prob=%.4f\n", output_value, probability);
   501→    }
   502→  } else if (output_tensor->type == kTfLiteInt8) {
   503→    int8_t output_value = output_tensor->data.int8[0];
   504→    probability = (output_value - output_tensor->params.zero_point) *
   505→                  output_tensor->params.scale;
   506→    if (++out_debug == 50) {
   507→      Serial.printf("Raw output int8=%d, prob=%.4f\n", output_value, probability);
   508→    }
   509→  } else {
   510→    probability = output_tensor->data.f[0];
   511→    if (++out_debug == 50) {
   512→      Serial.printf("Raw output float=%.4f\n", probability);
   513→    }
   514→  }
   515→
   516→  return probability;
   517→}
   518→
   519→bool detectWakeword(float probability) {
   520→  // Add to sliding window
   521→  probability_window[window_pos] = probability;
   522→  window_pos = (window_pos + 1) % SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;
   523→
   524→  if (window_pos == 0) {
   525→    window_filled = true;
   526→  }
   527→
   528→  // Don't trigger until window is filled
   529→  if (!window_filled) {
   530→    return false;
   531→  }
   532→
   533→  // Cooldown check - ignore detections for a period after last trigger
   534→  if (millis() - last_detection_ms < COOLDOWN_MS) {
   535→    return false;
   536→  }
   537→
   538→  // Calculate average probability AND count high frames
   539→  float avg = 0.0f;
   540→  int high_frames = 0;
   541→  for (int i = 0; i < SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE; i++) {
   542→    avg += probability_window[i];
   543→    if (probability_window[i] >= MIN_FRAME_PROB) {
   544→      high_frames++;
   545→    }
   546→  }
   547→  avg /= SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE;
   548→
   549→  // Log probability (always show for debugging)
   550→  static int log_count = 0;
   551→  if (probability > 0.01f || ++log_count >= 100) {
   552→    Serial.printf("prob: %.4f, avg: %.4f, high: %d/%d\n", probability, avg, high_frames, SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE);
   553→    log_count = 0;
   554→  }
   555→
   556→  // Require BOTH: high average AND sustained detection (filters partial words)
   557→  if (avg >= PROBABILITY_CUTOFF && high_frames >= MIN_HIGH_FRAMES) {
   558→    last_detection_ms = millis();  // Start cooldown
   559→    return true;
   560→  }
   561→  return false;
   562→}
   563→
   564→void errorBlink() {
   565→  while (1) {
   566→    digitalWrite(LED_PIN, !digitalRead(LED_PIN));
   567→    delay(200);
   568→  }
   569→}
